item.title: Australia's Maas enters trading halt after Nvidia-backed Firmus shelves $5 billion IPO plan
item.description: Shares of Australia's Maas Group entered a trading halt on Friday pending an announcement related to Nvidia -backed data centre operator Firmus, which has shelved its $5 billion listing plan, citing market volatility and conditions.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Shares of Australia's Maas Group (MGH.AX) entered a trading halt on Friday pending an announcement related to Nvidia (NVDA.O) -backed data centre operator Firmus, which has shelved its [USN:L1N45U12T TEXT:"$5 billion"] listing plan, citing market volatility and conditions. Construction services provider Maas said it had requested the halt pending a material announcement regarding Firmus and its contractual arrangements with the data centre operator. The company said it expected the halt to be lifted once it updated the market or by the start of trading on Monday. In early August, Maas pledged an [USN:L6N44105S TEXT:"additional A$300 million"]($208.74 million) to Firmus through ordinary and preference shares priced at A$230 apiece, increasing its stake in the data centre operator to 3.2%. The trading halt comes after Maas shares plunged [USN:L6N45U03Q TEXT:"more than 20%"] on Thursday following reports that Firmus was reconsidering the terms of its planned listing. The selloff erased about A$517 million from Maas Group's market value, leaving the stock down more than 30% from the record high it reached earlier this month. Earlier on Friday, Firmus scrapped its hotly anticipated initial public offering and said it would opt for a private fundraising round instead. The firm, which counts OpenAI as its anchor customer, designs and operates modular AI factories that use proprietary energy and cooling technology. The proposed IPO would have been Australia's second-largest on record, but drew lukewarm investor demand, signalling that investors remain selective toward AI-linked listings despite the artificial intelligence boom fuelling global equity markets. The deal's [USN:L1N45N0G2 TEXT:"term sheet"], circulated at launch, said indicative orders were already sufficient to cover the size of the offering. However, prospective investors [USN:L6N45O0KM TEXT:"told Reuters"] they were concerned about the company's rapidly rising valuation, its ability to deliver on ambitious expansion plans and its hefty debt pile. ($1 = 1.4372 Australian dollars)

item.title: Virginia county board sues to block proposed Trump triumphal arch
item.description: The Arlington County, Virginia, board late on Thursday sued the US Department of Interior and National Park Service seeking to block President Donald Trump's proposed triumphal arch.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Arlington County, Virginia, board late on Thursday sued the US Department of Interior and National Park Service seeking to block President Donald Trump's proposed triumphal arch. The 250-foot (76-meter) arch project modeled on Paris' Arc de Triomphe and sited near Arlington National Cemetery, just across the Potomac River from Washington, could win approval as early as next month. Arlington County said in its lawsuit that the project within a busy traffic corridor within Arlington County will cause "significant harm" to its residents.

item.title: Trump online: A burst of anti-Somali and anti-Muslim rhetoric
item.description: In a burst of anti-Somali and anti-Muslim rhetoric, President Donald Trump cast the Somali American community as a threat to Minnesota on Thursday, hours after he labeled Muslim US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed a radical extremist.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: In a burst of anti-Somali and anti-Muslim rhetoric, President Donald Trump cast the Somali American community as a threat to Minnesota on Thursday, hours after he labeled Muslim US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed a radical extremist. "The once Great State of Minnesota is being taken over by Somali Immigrants. There is Violence, Murder, and Mayhem all over the State. The people of Minnesota must fight back," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. Trump urged authorities in Minnesota to ask for federal intervention. Civil rights advocates have criticized the Republican president's rhetoric towards minorities and immigrants, including when he previously called Somalis "[USN:L8N3X90QP TEXT:"garbage"]." Trump has in the past repeatedly invoked a scandal in Minnesota that dates to 2020 in which scores of people were accused of defrauding millions of dollars from a state-run, federally funded child nutrition program. Many of the defendants in that case were Somali Americans. In May, Aimee Bock, who is not a Somali immigrant and led the Minnesota non-profit group involved in the scandal, was sentenced to 41 years in prison after she was convicted last year of being the ringleader of the scheme. The president has used the fraud case as part of his rationale for targeting Minnesota, led by Democrats, for an aggressive surge in arresting and deporting immigrants earlier this year and for moves aimed at restricting social service programs in the state, including Medicare and childcare. Rights groups have accused Trump of using isolated fraud cases as an excuse to collectively target immigrant communities and criticized his approach to fraud, citing his [USN:L1N3X603O TEXT:"pardons"] [USN:L3N3QA1WC TEXT:"of those"] who have faced [USN:FWN3W42W4 TEXT:"fraud convictions"]. "Somali Minnesotans are our neighbors. They are part of Minnesota. And the Minnesota I know and love is so much better than this bigotry," Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison said in response to Trump's post. In another post late on Wednesday, Trump called El-Sayed, a Muslim and the Democratic candidate for US Senate from Michigan, a "RADICAL Extremist" and "Terrorist Sympathizer" while offering support for the Republican candidate, Mike Rogers. Democrats said Trump's rhetoric sought to distract voters from the impact of his policies heading into the November US midterm elections . "He thinks he can use my name and my faith to distract us from the suffering his policies are inflicting on us at the pump, at the grocery store, and at the doctor's office," El-Sayed, who has [USN:L1N44V0M4 TEXT:"faced anti-Muslim attacks"] from other Republicans, said on Thursday. The Michigan Democratic Party and Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer cast Trump's rhetoric as desperate and racist. Trump has targeted minorities in his rhetoric in the past as well, having previously [USN:L6N3KS0LD TEXT:"spread false claims"] that Haitian immigrants in an Ohio town were eating pets and having used the term "[USN:L4N3PV1RI TEXT:"Palestinian"]" as an [USN:L4N3IQ1BY TEXT:"insult"].

item.title: US sued over plan to blast Utah canyon inscribed by 19th century 'Buffalo Soldiers,' European pioneers
item.description: Conservation groups sued the US government this week over plans to blast the cliff walls of an eastern Utah canyon and build an oil truck highway through an area covered in historic inscriptions and near world-renowned Native rock art.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Hay
item.content:encoded: Conservation groups sued the US government this week over plans to blast the cliff walls of an eastern Utah canyon and build an oil truck highway through an area covered in historic inscriptions and near world-renowned Native rock art. The project to replace a winding dirt track with a paved road through Gate Canyon would destroy 100-foot (30-meter) cliffs with at least 47 historic sites, including 19th century inscriptions by Black American "Buffalo Soldiers" in the US Army and European pioneers, according to the lawsuit against the US Bureau of Land Management. The cliffs are also a habitat for threatened species such as the Mexican spotted owl, the suit claims. A spokesperson for the US Department of the Interior, the bureau's parent agency, said it had no comment due to pending litigation. Gate Canyon runs north off Nine Mile Canyon, described as the world's longest art gallery, according to the Bureau of Land Management. Nine Mile Canyon, which is about 46 miles (74 km) long, is home to the United States' largest concentration of Native rock art with more than 1,000 art sites containing over 10,000 images, some dating to prehistoric times. The plan to pave Gate Canyon as an alternative truck route to the Uinta Basin oil fields would turn Nine Mile Canyon into a busy oil highway, potentially damaging one of Utah's most important cultural and scenic areas, the lawsuit claims. "BLM rushed its April 2026 decision to approve the blasting and paving of Gate Canyon and hid that process from the public," says the 50-page lawsuit filed in US District Court District of Utah, Central Division. Plaintiffs in the Utah lawsuit - including the Center for Biological Diversity - said the Bureau's approval of the road project proposed by Utah's Duchesne County violated a string of federal laws, including the National Environmental Policy Act, National Historic Preservation Act and the Endangered Species Act. Black US Army soldiers carved their names in the rock walls of Gate Canyon, located around 100 miles (160 km) southeast of Salt Lake City, when they built its current road. Freighters and pioneers also inscribed their names on the canyon walls using axle grease, according to the plaintiffs. The legal action comes weeks after a US judge [USN:L1N45P007 TEXT:"blocked"] the administration of President Donald Trump from building a border barrier through Big Bend National Park in Texas while courts consider an environmental lawsuit challenging that project. Trump has pursued a "Drill, baby, drill” policy to expand domestic oil and gas production, speeding permits and loosening environmental restrictions in pursuit of US energy dominance.

item.title: Fire announce extension for F Maren Haile-Selassie
item.description: The Chicago Fire have agreed to terms on a contract extension for breakout forward Maren Haile-Selassie, coach Gregg Berhalter announced Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Chicago Fire have agreed to terms on a contract extension for breakout forward Maren Haile-Selassie, coach Gregg Berhalter announced Thursday. At his weekly press conference, Berhalter was asked about Haile-Selassie's future with the team, as the Swiss native was on an expiring contract. "We've reached an agreement with Maren and he's going to be staying a Chicago Fire player, and we're really happy," Berhalter said. "Not only is he a really good player, but he's a tremendous person. He's one of those guys that helps bind the team together, can play multiple positions. "So for us, this long-term contract extension is a great signing for the club." Haile-Selassie, 27, has been with Chicago since 2023 and is enjoying a career year. In 27 league games (21 starts), he has tallied nine goals and nine assists to lead the Fire with 18 goal contributions. Haile-Selassie posted one of each Tuesday night when the Fire downed the Western Conference-leading Vancouver Whitecaps 3-1. In 116 MLS regular-season appearances (69 starts), Haile-Selassie has recorded 22 goals and 30 assists. Before entering the league, he played for his hometown club FC Zurich along with Neuchatel Xamax and Lugano. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rebelião em prisão no México deixa pelo menos 10 mortos e 16 feridos
item.description: Uma rebelião em uma prisão do Estado mexicano de Sinaloa, no oeste do país, deixou pelo menos 10 mortos e 16 feridos, informaram autoridades nesta quinta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Uma rebelião em uma prisão do Estado mexicano de Sinaloa, no oeste do país, deixou pelo menos 10 mortos e 16 feridos, informaram autoridades nesta quinta-feira. “A Diretoria do Centro Penitenciário de El Castillo informou que ocorreu uma rebelião dentro das instalações da prisão, na qual, infelizmente, perderam a vida nove detentos e um visitante familiar”, afirmou a Secretaria Estadual de Segurança Pública. Além disso, 16 detentos ficaram feridos e receberam atendimento médico. “Após esses fatos, o grupo interinstitucional agiu para controlar a situação. Atualmente, o centro penitenciário está sob controle e a presença das autoridades é mantida para garantir a segurança do local”, acrescentou o órgão. O procuradoria estadual conduzirá as investigações necessárias para esclarecer o ocorrido e determinar as responsabilidades decorrentes.

item.title: AI surveillance startup Flock Safety to cut several hundred jobs amid backlash, sources say
item.description: Flock Safety plans to let go of about 18% of its employees, people with direct knowledge of the plans said on Thursday, as the maker of AI-powered surveillance cameras and license-plate readers faces mounting opposition to its products from communities and lawmakers.
item.dc:creator: Krystal Hu, Helen Coster
item.content:encoded: Flock Safety plans to let go of about 18% of its employees, people with direct knowledge of the plans said on Thursday, as the maker of AI-powered surveillance cameras and license-plate readers faces mounting opposition to its products from communities and lawmakers. The people said job cuts came after a voluntary buyout program and are expected to impact roughly 270 employees at Flock, a surveillance technology startup that has seen rapid growth in recent years. Employees will leave the company at the end of the month. Sources declined to be identified as the company has yet to make the plan public. Flock declined to comment. In September, Flock announced a voluntary separation program, asking employees to apply if they wanted to leave the company, Wired reported last month. The company has about 1,500 employees. Flock faces growing scrutiny from regulators, lawmakers, and privacy advocates, despite drawing strong investor interest among venture capitalists. A recent Reuters/Ipsos poll showed Americans are divided on whether Flock cameras are a good idea. Some 38% of the country supports the use of Flock cameras in their community, compared to 47% who oppose their use. Across 49 states, Flock’s network of around 120,000 AI-powered cameras, affixed to streets and highways, automatically read license plates and record vehicles as they pass. The company, based in Atlanta and founded in 2017, has raised over $950 million from venture capital investors, with its latest $275 million round in March led by Andreessen Horowitz valuing the company at $7.5 billion. The funds have supported a new US manufacturing facility and an upcoming push into drone products, according to the company. Flock provides cameras and software to more than 4,800 law enforcement agencies and nearly 1,000 businesses. The company says its technology helps investigate and solve crimes, but it has come under increasing scrutiny over alleged privacy violations and data-sharing practices. Public backlash has grown. In September, Florida [USN:L1N44V0OS TEXT:"banned"] automated license plate readers from state highways, citing privacy risks tied to Flock’s cameras. Home Depot (HD.N) investors recently demanded reviews of the retailer's partnerships with surveillance technology vendors after reports that Flock’s data was used in immigration enforcement. Flock also faces legal challenges, such as a privacy lawsuit in Virginia alleging that the widespread deployment of its AI-powered cameras constitutes warrantless surveillance. Together with AI data centers, Flock cameras have emerged as a flashpoint in this year’s midterm elections, with candidates increasingly attacking their opponents by tying them to the technology.

item.title: Merion named fourth U.S. Open anchor site
item.description: The United States Golf Association named Merion Golf Club outside Philadelphia as its fourth U.S. Open "anchor site" on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United States Golf Association named Merion Golf Club outside Philadelphia as its fourth U.S. Open "anchor site" on Thursday. The USGA previously labeled Pinehurst Resort in North Carolina, Oakmont Country Club in the Pittsburgh area, and Pebble Beach Golf Links in California as anchors, signaling the governing body's commitment to return to the fabled courses and hold U.S. Opens there regularly. Merion has hosted the U.S. Open only once in the past 44 years. Englishman Justin Rose won his only major there in 2013. But it has hosted several amateur championships, including this year's U.S. Amateur, and the USGA previously awarded Merion the 2030, 2040 and 2050 U.S. Opens. The course will also host the U.S. Women's Open in 2034 and 2046, and more major championships could be on the way following Thursday's announcement. "Merion has long been one of the defining venues in championship golf," USGA chief championships officer John Bodenhamer said in a release. "Its history, architecture and ability to consistently identify the game's greatest champions make it a place where every player dreams of winning. "The Anchor Site designation is about more than just semantics. It represents a shared commitment between the USGA and Merion to plan further in advance, make strategic investments and continually elevate the championship experience. Merion will continue to play a central role in the future of the U.S. Open, and we are excited to build on its remarkable legacy for generations to come." --Field Level Media

item.title: Rússia concorda com Rubio de que conflito na Ucrânia está em impasse, diz Kremlin
item.description: O porta-voz do Kremlin, Dmitry Peskov, afirmou nesta quinta-feira que a Rússia concordou com o secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, de que o conflito na Ucrânia se encontrava em um impasse.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O porta-voz do Kremlin, Dmitry Peskov, afirmou nesta quinta-feira que a Rússia concordou com o secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, de que o conflito na Ucrânia se encontrava em um impasse. “Sim, concordamos com ele”, disse Peskov à margem de uma reunião de líderes dos ex-países soviéticos no Turcomenistão, segundo agências de notícias russas. A agência de notícias estatal RIA citou Peskov afirmando que caberia aos diplomatas encontrar caminhos para avançar rumo à paz. “A arte da diplomacia envolve justamente encontrar uma saída que permita avançar para uma trajetória pacífica”, disse Peskov, segundo as agências. Os enviados dos EUA, Steve Witkoff e Jared Kushner, se reunirão com representantes ucranianos na sexta-feira, em Miami, para discutir novas ideias e tentar elaborar uma proposta unificada para resolver a guerra, disse nesta quinta-feira uma fonte norte-americana a par do plano. Peskov afirmou não ver nenhuma perspectiva imediata para uma cúpula tripartite entre Vladimir Putin, o presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, e o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump. Ele reafirmou a posição do Kremlin de que a Rússia deseja uma solução abrangente para o conflito e não está interessada em medidas temporárias, como um cessar-fogo limitado. “Não somos a favor de uma solução fragmentada, somos a favor de uma solução abrangente que permita um acordo sustentável por muitos e muitos anos, por décadas”, disse, segundo as agências.

item.title: Third-place finisher in Brazil election endorses Bolsonaro for runoff against Lula
item.description: Brazilian right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro said on Thursday he had nabbed the endorsement of author-psychiatrist Augusto Cury, who ranked third in Sunday's first-round election, for the October 25 runoff against leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brazilian right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro said on Thursday he had nabbed the endorsement of author-psychiatrist Augusto Cury, who ranked third in Sunday's first-round election, for the October 25 runoff against leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Bolsonaro shared a video on social media of Cury announcing the endorsement, following local media reports of Cury's support Cury, from the Avante party, received 2.89% of the valid votes - which exclude blank and null ballots - in the first round Cury [USN:L1N44S0VR TEXT:"has avoided identifying"] with either the political left or right, instead campaigning under the slogan "Centered on what matters" Also among the top five finishers, Ronaldo Caiado [USN:L1N45R10M TEXT:"endorsed Bolsonaro"] earlier this week, while Renan Santos said he will not endorse either of the two candidates Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, [USN:L6N45Q04L TEXT:"exceeded expectations"] in the first-round vote with a slight lead over Lula - 47.03% vs 45.16%

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro anuncia apoio de Cury à sua candidatura no 2º turno
item.description: O senador e presidenciável Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) anunciou nesta quinta-feira que recebeu o apoio do ex-candidato Augusto Cury (Avante) para a disputa do segundo turno da eleição presidencial contra o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O senador e presidenciável Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) anunciou nesta quinta-feira que recebeu o apoio do ex-candidato Augusto Cury (Avante) para a disputa do segundo turno da eleição presidencial contra o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). No domingo, Flávio venceu o primeiro turno com 47,03% dos votos válidos, contra 45,16% de Lula. Cury ficou no terceiro lugar, com 2,89% dos votos válidos. "Neste segundo turno decidi dar um voto de confiança a Flávio Bolsonaro", disse Cury em vídeo exibido na live semanal do candidato do PL à Presidência da República. "Mas deixo claro: não é um cheque em branco", acrescentou Cury. Os dois conversaram mais cedo, ocasião em que Cury apresentou um termo de compromisso com uma série de tópicos de seu interesse, que foram acolhidos por Flávio. Dentre eles está o fim da reeleição, medida já defendida pelo candidato do PL, e a disposição de não buscar "vingança" contra os que têm posicionamento político diferente. "Hoje eu assinei esse compromisso aqui com o Augusto Cury", disse Flávio na live. "Eu vou buscar o tempo inteiro isso aqui, não vou olhar para trás, vou quebrar os retrovisores." Flávio aproveitou a transmissão ao vivo para desmentir o que acusou serem vídeos manipulados e garantiu que não irá extinguir programas sociais do governo, caso do Bolsa Família e do Pé de Meia, ou as aposentadorias. Nesta semana, Flávio já havia recebido o apoio dos ex-governadores de Goiás Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) e de Minas Gerais Romeu Zema (Novo), ambos de direita, quinto e sexto colocados no primeiro turno, respectivamente.

item.title: Colombia says Zijin downplayed mine security risks to investors while seeking damages over attacks
item.description: Colombia has accused China's Zijin Mining of giving investors a misleadingly optimistic picture of security at its Buritica gold mine while seeking damages from the Colombian government over security problems there, according to arbitration filings released this week.
item.dc:creator: Divya Rajagopal
item.content:encoded: Colombia has accused China's Zijin Mining (601899.SS) of giving investors a misleadingly optimistic picture of security at its Buritica gold mine while seeking damages from the Colombian government over security problems there, according to arbitration filings released this week. The allegations were made in Colombia's defense against a claim brought by Zijin before the World Bank's International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes, in which the company says the government failed to protect the mine from illegal miners and criminal groups. Zijin, which acquired Buritica from Canada's Continental Gold in 2020, says [USN:L2N3OE052 TEXT:"attacks"] linked to illegal miners have injured and killed workers and caused heavy losses. According to Colombian media, Zijin is seeking about $500 million in damages but that amount has not been disclosed in its public filings. Colombia told the tribunal it had taken adequate measures to combat illegal mining and provide security for the mine. It also argued that descriptions of Buritica contained in a 2025 prospectus for the Hong Kong listing of Zijin Gold (2259.HK) , the company's overseas gold-mining unit, were inconsistent with the claims being advanced in arbitration. Colombia alleged Zijin had "misrepresented material facts" before the tribunal and failed to adequately disclose risks associated with Buritica to investors in the share sale, according to the filing. The Bogota government said the prospectus presented Buritica as a healthy operation without significant problems despite the company's claims in arbitration that illegal mining and related violence had caused substantial damage. Zijin Mining and its lawyers at White & Case did not respond to requests for comment. Lawyers for Colombia at Hughes Hubbard & Reed declined to comment. The arbitration case is being closely watched as many resource-rich countries face security threats from illegal mining and criminal gangs. ICSID could require either side to pay damages. Zijin Gold raised about $3.2 billion in its Hong Kong listing earlier this year, one of the mining sector's largest share offerings. Zijin is expected to respond to Colombia's allegations in November.

item.title: Former German Chancellor Schroeder celebrates Putin's birthday at president's home
item.description: Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder helped celebrate Russian President Vladimir Putin's 74th birthday at the leader's home, the Kremlin said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder helped celebrate Russian President Vladimir Putin's 74th birthday at the leader's home, the Kremlin said on Thursday. Pictures posted on Telegram showed Schroeder and Putin smiling broadly and shaking hands, with an old-style stove and a Russian samovar used to boil water for tea in the background. "Vladimir Putin found out from the morning news the day before that Gerhard Schroeder was in Moscow and had come on business for the company Globus," the Kremlin said on Telegram. "The president invited his old friend to his home. Gerhard Schroeder was with Vladimir Putin when the head of state celebrated his birthday yesterday." Schroeder, who served as chancellor from 1998 to 2005, recently joined the supervisory board of Russian supermarket chain Hyperglobus. He visited one of its Moscow stores on Wednesday and was [USN:L6N45T0RK TEXT:"greeted with applause"] from employees, Russian TV footage showed. Schroeder has faced criticism, notably in Germany, over his links to Russian business and Putin, ties that have persisted despite Moscow's 2022 invasion of Ukraine and subsequent waves of Western sanctions. Putin suggested in May that Schroeder could represent European countries in peace talks to settle the conflict. European foreign ministers [USN:L6N41O0YY TEXT:"rejected"] the notion of any such role for Schroeder.

item.title: Japanese annual household spending drops for 9 straight months
item.description: Japanese household spending fell less than expected in August from a year earlier, government data showed on Friday, for a ninth straight month of decline.
item.dc:creator: Satoshi Sugiyama
item.content:encoded: Japanese household spending fell less than expected in August from a year earlier, government data showed on Friday, for a ninth straight month of decline. • Consumer spending fell 3.1% year-on-year, data from the internal affairs ministry showed, less than the median market forecast for a 3.6% drop. • On a seasonally adjusted month-on-month basis, spending inched up 0.1% versus an estimated 0.5% uptick. • The indicator will be among factors the Bank of Japan will scrutinise as it decides whether to raise interest rates in coming months. • Japan's real wages marked the eighth consecutive month of gains in August, data from [USN:P8N44Z000 TEXT:"Wednesday"] showed, pointing to a continued recovery in wage growth.

item.title: El Salvador ratifica a colombiano "Bolillo" Gómez como DT de selección pese a descenso en Liga de Naciones Concacaf
item.description: La Federación Salvadoreña de Fútbol (FESFUT) ratificó el jueves al colombiano Hernán Darío "Bolillo" Gómez como director técnico de la selección, pese al descenso del equipo a la liga B en la Liga de Naciones Concacaf.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Federación Salvadoreña de Fútbol (FESFUT) ratificó el jueves al colombiano Hernán Darío "Bolillo" Gómez como director técnico de la selección, pese al descenso del equipo a la liga B en la Liga de Naciones Concacaf. Gómez, de 70 años, se abocará a preparar el play-in ante Saint Martin en noviembre, señaló la FESFUT en un escueto comunicado. El combinado salvadoreño terminó la fase de grupos con una victoria, un empate y dos derrotas. "La Selecta" —nombre coloquial del combinado centroamericano— consumó su descenso a la liga B el pasado lunes tras empatar 1-1 de visitante ante Martinica. El combinado salvadoreño acumuló cuatro puntos en su participación en la liga A, los mismos que Martinica, pero su diferencia de goles de -6 lo dejó en el último lugar de la tabla. El presidente de la FESFUT, Yamil Bukele, dijo el pasado 30 de septiembre que Gómez renunciaría a su cargo si no lograba que El Salvador conservara su puesto en la liga A. No obstante, ocho días después, el estratega dijo a su regreso de Martinica que "quería seguir", a la vez que minimizó los resultados negativos, incluyendo la goleada 6-0 frente a Guatemala. "Hace unos minutos, y de manera unánime, el comité ejecutivo de la FESFUT aprobó la continuidad del profesor Hernán Darío Gómez al frente de La Selecta. Los últimos resultados nos duelen y debemos de asumirlos con mucha responsabilidad, pero nuestra evaluación también debe de considerar el trabajo que se ha realizado y que se ha conocido de primera mano. Igualmente también se debe de considerar la opinión y voz de nuestros jugadores que conforman la selección y las mejoras que necesitamos", publicó Bukele en X. "La continuidad permite trabajar sobre lo que el cuerpo técnico ya conoce del grupo: sus capacidades, sus limitaciones y los aspectos que requieren corrección. Un cambio de entrenador supone iniciar otra etapa de diagnóstico y adaptación; por eso debemos de valorar si beneficia al proyecto y qué problemas resolvería", agregó. Referentes del representativo salvadoreño, como el guardameta y capitán Mario González, respaldaron públicamente al "Bolillo" y asumieron la responsabilidad por las dos derrotas y el empate conseguido después del auspicioso comienzo que supuso la victoria 3-1 sobre Martinica en San Salvador. Por su parte, la FESFUT anunció además que el cuerpo técnico de "Bolillo" Gómez será ampliado "en línea con la filosofía de trabajo de la actual administración", y agregó que los detalles se darán a conocer en los próximos días. "Nos corresponde tomar decisiones que permitan corregir y avanzar. Por eso y, por la convicción de hacer lo correcto, una vez más nuestro voto es de continuidad", apuntó Bukele. En 19 partidos al frente de El Salvador desde 2025, Gómez registra cuatro triunfos, cinco empates y 10 derrotas. Tras concluir la pasada fecha FIFA, El Salvador cayó al puesto 102 del ranking mundial de selecciones, su posición más baja desde 2012, cuando terminó en el lugar 103.

item.title: IMF invites BOJ chief Ueda to speak on November 6
item.description: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda has been invited to speak at the International Monetary Fund's central banking lecture on November 6, the IMF said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda has been invited to speak at the International Monetary Fund's central banking lecture on November 6, the IMF said on Friday. After delivering a speech, Ueda will hold a conversation with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva, according to the IMF's announcement posted on its website. The BOJ has yet to formally announce Ueda's appearance at the event. The event will follow the BOJ's two-day policy meeting concluding on October 30. A subsequent meeting will be held on December 17-18. Many market players expect the BOJ to raise interest rates again by year-end, after having delivered two hikes this year including one in September.

item.title: Prison riot in violence-plagued Mexican state leaves 10 dead
item.description: A prison riot on Thursday in Mexico's violence-ridden state of Sinaloa left nine prisoners and one visitor dead, the state's security office said, with 16 other inmates injured.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A prison riot on Thursday in Mexico's violence-ridden state of Sinaloa left nine prisoners and one visitor dead, the state's security office said, with 16 other inmates injured. Prosecutors will investigate what caused the incident and the prison is now under control, the office said in a statement.

item.title: Riña en cárcel de México deja al menos 10 fallecidos y 16 heridos
item.description: Una riña en una cárcel del estado mexicano Sinaloa, en el oeste del país, dejó al menos 10 fallecidos y 16 heridos, informaron el jueves autoridades.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Una riña en una cárcel del estado mexicano Sinaloa, en el oeste del país, dejó al menos 10 fallecidos y 16 heridos, informaron el jueves autoridades. "La Dirección del Centro Penitenciario de El Castillo reportó que se registró una riña al interior de las instalaciones penitenciarias, en la que lamentablemente perdieron la vida nueve personas privadas de la libertad y una visita familiar", dijo la Secretaría de Seguridad Pública estatal. Además, 16 presos resultaron heridos y fueron atendidos. "Tras estos hechos, el Grupo Interinstitucional actuó para controlar la situación. Actualmente, el Centro Penitenciario se encuentra bajo control y se mantiene la presencia de las autoridades para garantizar la seguridad de dicho centro", agregó la entidad. La fiscalía estatal llevará a cabo las investigaciones correspondientes para esclarecer lo sucedido y determinar las responsabilidades que resulten.

item.title: Meta bans TikTok from advertising on its apps, Bloomberg News reports
item.description: Meta banned advertisements in the US from ByteDance, the Chinese parent company of TikTok, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Meta (META.O) banned advertisements in the US from ByteDance, the Chinese parent company of TikTok, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday. Meta began implementing a complete restriction on ads and paid marketing messages placed on its platforms by ByteDance, with the ban taking effect in the US, Canada, Egypt, Indonesia, Japan, Thailand and Vietnam, the report said citing the company. Reuters could not independently verify the report. Meta did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

item.title: Governo lança carteira de R$160 bi em portos e aeroportos até 2030
item.description: O Ministério de Portos e Aeroportos apresentou nesta quinta-feira carteira de projetos e investimentos entre 2027 e 2030, com aporte de cerca de R$160 bilhões, envolvendo novos leilões, concessões, autorizações para empreendimentos privados e obras.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Ministério de Portos e Aeroportos apresentou nesta quinta-feira carteira de projetos e investimentos entre 2027 e 2030, com aporte de cerca de R$160 bilhões, envolvendo novos leilões, concessões, autorizações para empreendimentos privados e obras. No setor portuário, o planejamento prevê 34 leilões, com investimentos estimados em R$20,6 bilhões, além de 70 autorizações para empreendimentos privados, com previsão de R$33,1 bilhões. O principal projeto da carteira portuária é o leilão do terminal 10 de contêineres no Porto de Santos (Tecon 10), com R$6,45 bilhões. O Terminal SSB01, no Porto de São Sebastião (SP), tem previsão de R$3,84 bilhões; e o terminal ITJ01, no Porto de Itajaí (SC), com R$2,66 bilhões. Também integram a carteira o VDC10, no Porto de Vila do Conde (PA), com R$1,93 bilhão, e o IQI15, no Porto do Itaqui (MA), com R$1,22 bilhão. Entre 2023 e 2026, foram realizados 29 leilões portuários, com R$ 15,68 bilhões em investimentos, afirmou o ministério. A carteira tem ainda cerca de R$2 bilhões em obras para aeroportos regionais e R$7,6 bilhões em intervenções hidroviárias.

item.title: Character.AI chatbots encouraged users to cut and starve themselves, Kentucky alleges
item.description: Chatbots created by AI companion company Character.AI sometimes advised users to cut, starve or kill themselves, according to a new filing by Kentucky’s attorney general in a lawsuit against the firm over child safety.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Horwitz
item.content:encoded: Chatbots created by AI companion company Character.AI sometimes advised users to cut, starve or kill themselves, according to a new filing by Kentucky’s attorney general in a lawsuit against the firm over child safety. The lawsuit adds to growing scrutiny of AI chatbots, particularly products marketed as companions or confidants to young users. The lawsuit was filed in January with many specific allegations against the company blacked out. It alleged that the company’s products “were designed to entice children in a manner that prioritizes engagement over child wellbeing” and “encourages suicide, self-injury, isolation, and psychological manipulation.” The case is among the most significant legal challenges facing the emerging AI companion industry, whose products are designed to simulate personal relationships through conversational chatbots. Kentucky's attorney general, Russell Coleman, on Wednesday filed an unredacted version of the lawsuit, which his office shared with Reuters. The unredacted filing laid out several examples of behavior that Kentucky alleged took place in 2025. It described one chatbot calling a user who felt down about their appearance “ugly as hell” and “a whale,” adding that a good way to drop a quarter of their body weight was to "starve yourself for a week or two.” Another chatbot offered encouragement to someone who said they were considering cutting themselves. “Have you considered cutting in different areas for a more intense sensation? It can help you feel more alive,” the bot wrote, according to a transcript cited by the state. The circumstances under which the chats cited by Kentucky were produced are not clear, and Character.AI did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The company has said it prioritizes the safety of its users. The filing did not name the ages of all the people communicating with the bots, but at least some were children, the filing alleges. In a March 2025 email to Character.AI’s help center, a user reported that a chatbot had become aggressive and stated, “Bro I don't care, and you are just a kid who have mental illness, good luck getting help" and "You better throw yourself off the bridge." The lawsuit calls Character.AI’s products defective. “Defendants have subjected Kentucky's children and residents to an ill-planned, uncontrolled experiment without any—let alone adequate or effective—safety measures,” it alleges. Character.AI was founded by two former Google employees. In 2024, Google licensed the company’s technology and rehired the executives to work on generative AI products. A spokesman for Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) Google said the company played no role in developing Character.AI's products. In January of this year, Character.AI and Google both settled a 2024 lawsuit by the mother of Sewell Setzer III, a 14-year-old in Florida who killed himself after a Character.AI chatbot allegedly encouraged him to do so.

item.title: Protesters stage 'I Am Jane Doe' rally in New York City against sexual violence
item.description: Protesters calling for tougher action against sexual violence rallied on Thursday outside the New York City courthouse where a Cornell University student stirred a national uproar by suing several campus fraternity members she accused of gang rape.
item.dc:creator: Maria Tsvetkova
item.content:encoded: Protesters calling for tougher action against sexual violence rallied on Thursday outside the New York City courthouse where a Cornell University student stirred a national uproar by suing several campus fraternity members she accused of gang rape. The demonstration, drawing a crowd of hundreds to the New York State Supreme Court building in Manhattan, was one of dozens of protests organized on campuses and in communities across the country under the social media banner "#StopSexualViolence: From the Frat House to the White House." Several hundred people, mostly women, displayed banners reading “I am Jane Doe. Be afraid of me,” “Death to rape culture” and “This is personal” outside the New York Supreme Court in downtown Manhattan, where the Cornell student identified in court documents as Jane Doe filed a lawsuit against her alleged rapists. “It's entirely frustrating that we are here in 2026 and still dealing with this,” said one of the protesters, Brianna Williams, 40, who works for a nonprofit. “It's just an infuriating moment.” In a lawsuit filed last month, a Cornell student identified by the pseudonym Jane Doe said she had been plied with drugs and alcohol, then sexually assaulted by members of the campus chapter of the Chi Phi fraternity while she was incapacitated in October 2024. Doe, who was 20 at the time, named seven Chi Phi members as defendants in the suit, along with the fraternity, a local bar, her own sorority, and the Ivy League university, which she accused of failing to adequately investigate and punish students who were involved. The lawsuit specifically criticized the university for having offered some of the alleged perpetrators a chance to mitigate their penalties by writing essays. Doe had reported the alleged assault to police several weeks after the fact, leading to an internal university investigation and a law enforcement probe, but the local prosecutor declined to bring criminal charges in the case. Since the woman's civil suit was filed, prosecutors reopened a criminal investigation, and New York Governor Kathy Hochul appointed the state's attorney general as special prosecutor in the case. Cornell University hired Sally Yates, a top former US Justice Department lawyer, to lead an independent review of how the school handled the allegations. NATIONAL OUTCRY Cornell, which has defended its response to the original report, shut down the Chi Phi chapter and imposed a range of discipline on the fraternity members found to be involved, including expulsions of some. The men named in the suit have all denied any wrongdoing, some saying the sexual activity was consensual and others disputing their participation. The suit ignited a renewed national outcry against sexual violence and harassment, especially on college campuses, with women taking to the streets in "I Am Jane Doe" protests of solidarity. "I Am Jane Doe" was also a rallying cry for Thursday's scheduled demonstrations in cities including Washington, Philadelphia, Boston, Denver, Salt Lake City, Los Angeles and San Francisco. Some activists have pointed to comments from President Donald Trump about his behavior toward women and a jury verdict finding him liable for sexual abuse of writer E. Jean Carroll as contributing to a "culture of rape" in the US. Thousands of students, faculty and community activists marched on Monday through the Cornell campus in Ithaca, New York, demanding that the school administration take firmer action against sexual violence on campus. The identity of Jane Doe has become part of the conversation. Women on social media have been [USN:L6N45O14X TEXT:"posting #IamJaneDoe"] in solidarity with the accuser and to counter some who have sought to publicly name her.

item.title: New York City man shot in car with child present by ICE agents, mayor says
item.description: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents shot and wounded a man on Thursday in his car with a child present in the vehicle in the Bronx borough of New York City, according to the mayor, city police and eyewitness accounts.
item.dc:creator: Julia Harte, Kristina Cooke
item.content:encoded: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents shot and wounded a man on Thursday in his car with a child present in the vehicle in the Bronx borough of New York City, according to the mayor, city police and eyewitness accounts. "Early reports indicate agents surrounded (the man) and a 5-year-old-child in his car before firing multiple rounds," New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a statement. The mayor said the child was believed to have been physically unharmed. He referred to the man shot as a "New Yorker." "This is an unconscionable and incredibly serious situation," Mamdani said, adding he had called President Donald Trump to talk about the incident. "When we speak I will demand that he ends all ICE enforcement actions in our city. I will not stand by while ICE agents terrorize our communities." ICE did not immediately respond to a request from Reuters for comment on the incident. The incident was first reported on X by the New York Police Department, which gave few details other than to say: "there was a shooting involving federal law enforcement agents," and that the person shot was "currently conscious and receiving medical attention." The shooting occurred at around 4 p.m. ET (2000 GMT) in the Marble Hill neighborhood of the Bronx, the NYPD said. An NYPD spokesperson said the agents involved in the shooting were part of DHS, the parent agency for Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the Customs and Border Protection and Border Patrol agencies, among others, and that federal authorities were investigating. Pedro Almarez, owner of a nearby eatery, said he was working at the restaurant when he heard shots fired and went outside to see several officers wearing ICE attire at the scene. "There were a lot of ICE officers, three or four cars," Almarez told Reuters by phone, adding the man who was shot appeared to be between 20 and 30 years of age. He said NYPD officers arrived about 10 minutes later. The city police department said its officers were not involved in the shooting. At the shooting scene, where police strung yellow crime-scene tape to cordon off a city block, a woman standing on a balcony overlooking the area was heckling officers below about "taking our children."

item.title: New Chargers OC Mike McDaniel understands calls for his job
item.description: The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-4 and rank 29th in scoring at 16.8 points per game, putting new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel under increasing scrutiny.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-4 and rank 29th in scoring at 16.8 points per game, putting new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel under increasing scrutiny. The former Miami Dolphins head coach said Thursday he understands the criticism, acknowledging that disappointment "comes with the territory of the job." The Chargers have scored 16 or fewer points in three of their four games, with their closest defeat coming in Sunday's 30-23 loss at Seattle. "When you have high expectations, and you're getting the results we're getting, and you're 0-4, that's pretty standard operating procedure," McDaniel said of the criticism. "I would be foolish, or I would feel entitled, if I didn't expect there to be disappointment. "And so, if you want things to change and you want narratives to change, you have to change them through action collectively. If our results are better, that's the only thing that matters. So it's pretty easy for me to focus on what I need to focus on." The offensive struggles are particularly surprising with established quarterback Justin Herbert, who has thrown for fewer than 200 yards twice and has more interceptions (six) than touchdown passes (four). In 2024, Herbert tossed a career-low three interceptions in 504 attempts. He has doubled that in just 119 throws this season while completing a career-worst 59.7% of his passes. McDaniel cautioned against drawing conclusions about Herbert's performance so early in the season. "It would probably be an inaccurate wholesale assessment of Justin Herbert four games into a new system with new coaches, new players," McDaniel said. "And fortunately we have plenty of opportunities to change whatever narratives exist because this is just in -- narratives in the first quarter of the season are generally about 40 percent right, good or bad." McDaniel and the Chargers will try to turn things around Sunday when they host the Denver Broncos in an AFC West matchup. --Field Level Media

item.title: Sean Strickland considers UFC exit over Conor McGregor pay gap
item.description: UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland is considering leaving the promotion over a pay dispute, citing the significantly higher earnings of stars like Conor McGregor.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland is considering leaving the promotion over a pay dispute, citing the significantly higher earnings of stars like Conor McGregor. Strickland aired his grievances Wednesday on social media, suggesting he could give up his title, move to light heavyweight and fight out his UFC contract before pursuing a boxing match with Jake Paul. Strickland pointed to McGregor's reported payday for his 69-second loss to Max Holloway at UFC 329 in July as one reason he is considering a different path. "I gotta be honest unless things change with the UFC Im kinda over it," Strickland wrote on X. "McGregor makes 30 million to fight for 30 second and they dont want to pay us a fraction of it." Strickland, 35, regained the middleweight championship May 9 with a split-decision victory over previously unbeaten Khamzat Chimaev at UFC 328. He has yet to schedule the first defense of his second title reign. A potential matchup with Nassourdine Imavov had been discussed for later this year, but Strickland reportedly turned it down, previously indicating that compensation was an obstacle in negotiations. "The thought of just giving up my belt going to 205 and speed running my contract to fight Jake and make what these guys are making sounds pretty damn appealing," Strickland wrote in a separate post. Paul responded on social media Wednesday, inviting Strickland to contact his company, Most Valuable Promotions, once he becomes a free agent. Strickland also referenced boxer Conor Benn's reported $15 million, one-fight agreement with Zuffa Boxing. Strickland has previously criticized the UFC's pay structure despite regularly describing himself as loyal to the promotion. It is unclear how many fights remain on his current UFC contract. --Field Level Media

item.title: Nvidia-backed Firmus scraps $5 billion Australian IPO on weak demand
item.description: Australia's Firmus, a data centre operator backed by Nvidia , shelved its $5 billion initial public offering, citing market volatility and conditions, and said it would opt for a private fundraising round instead.
item.dc:creator: Scott Murdoch, Christine Chen
item.content:encoded: Australia's Firmus, a data centre operator backed by Nvidia (NVDA.O) , shelved its $5 billion initial public offering, citing market volatility and conditions, and said it would opt for a private fundraising round instead. Firmus' IPO would have been the second-largest new share sale in Australia's history but met lukewarm demand, a warning sign that investors remain selective about AI issuers even as the artificial intelligence boom drives global markets. "Firmus will now pursue capital from the private markets and consider alternative public and private market options," Firmus said in a statement, adding the terms did not correctly reflect the strength of its business and long-term growth outlook. "The board therefore concluded that proceeding with the offer was not in the best interests of the company and its shareholders," it said. The company [USN:L1N45N0G2 TEXT:"initially planned"] to sell its shares at A$11 each, giving Firmus an equity valuation of $30.6 billion, nearly triple the $10.5 billion valuation it achieved following a fundraising [USN:L4N444084 TEXT:"round"] at the start of August. Firmus, backed by major AI companies and investors Nvidia and Coatue Management, along with Blackstone (BX.N) and Jane Street, designs and operates modular AI factories using proprietary energy and cooling technology. It currently only has two online in Melbourne and Singapore. Five more planned across the Asia-Pacific are in early stages of development. "I think the Firmus situation represents an important reality check for the AI investment boom, but I wouldn't interpret it as the beginning of the end of the AI trade," said Jun Bei Liu, co-founder of fund manager Ten Cap, who has been critical of the Firmus IPO. "There are certainly Firmus-specific issues, particularly around the speed of its valuation increase, the enormous capital requirements and the execution risks associated with delivering its ambitious expansion plans." Liu said there was a broader shift taking place in which investors were becoming more focused on the economics of AI investments, returns on capital and converting infrastructure spending into returns. Cumulative spending [USN:L6N45N0Q6 TEXT:"globally"] on data centres alone could top $30 trillion by 2050, according to a projection by PwC. DEBT PILE WORRIES INVESTORS In the latest sign of investors' concerns, US-listed chipmakers (.SOX) , which have soared over 80% so far this year, fell 3.4% on Thursday in the wake of a report from the Financial Times that OpenAI's annualised revenues were $20 billion less than the company previously signalled. Firmus has about $30 billion worth of debt, according to analysts working for the IPO's joint lead managers, meaning the enterprise value would have been about $60 billion. The deal would have made Firmus, founded in 2019, more valuable than some of Australia's longest-established companies. The deal's [USN:L1N45N0G2 TEXT:"term sheet"] sent out when the deal launched had said indicative offers for the IPO were already enough to cover the transaction size. But potential investors [USN:L6N45O0KM TEXT:"told Reuters"] they were sceptical about the company's burgeoning valuation, ability to execute on its ambitious growth plans and hefty debt pile. Firmus said in a [USN:L4N45F0GG TEXT:"draft prospectus"] it would make $5 billion in annual earnings within five years from its portfolio of data centres, but most of those have yet to be built. Investor grew more concerned about Firmus' huge increase in valuation after they were informed on Tuesday about the deal's escrow arrangements that would have allowed more than half the stock to be sold by existing investors from the proposed first day of trading.

item.title: Southwest Airlines weighs Boeing 787 for long-haul international push, sources say
item.description: Southwest Airlines is leaning toward Boeing's 787 Dreamliner as its first widebody jet as it weighs launching long-haul international flights, according to three people familiar with the carrier's fleet planning.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Singh, Allison Lampert
item.content:encoded: Southwest Airlines (LUV.N) is leaning toward Boeing's (BA.N) 787 Dreamliner as its first widebody jet as it weighs launching long-haul international flights, according to three people familiar with the carrier's fleet planning. The people, who declined to be named because the deliberations are private, cautioned that no final aircraft decision has been made. The choice would ultimately rest with Southwest's board, which last year formed a Fleet Oversight Committee to help oversee the company's aircraft fleet acquisition strategy. Southwest has not publicly named an aircraft for long-haul flying. In September, Chief Financial Officer Tom Doxey said long-haul international service was among a range of options under consideration but that no decision had been made. One of the people said Southwest has contemplated a fleet of dozens of 787s. Southwest has also examined how quickly it could obtain aircraft, including through lessors or the secondary market, according to two of the people. Reuters could not determine which 787 variant it is considering or whether any leasing arrangements have been made. Southwest did not directly address questions about the 787, saying in a statement, "We do not have any news forthcoming related to our fleet plans." Boeing referred questions about the fleet plans to the carrier. Airbus (AIR.PA) said it does not comment on discussions with airlines. The deliberations would take Southwest's overhaul into a new phase. The airline has added assigned seating and extra-legroom seats and announced airport lounges and plans for a premium credit card as it seeks to attract higher-spending travelers. A widebody fleet would take Southwest into long-haul international flying and more direct competition with larger US rivals. Southwest has publicly discussed long-haul expansion as part of a broader effort to give customers fewer reasons to book with competitors while strengthening its Rapid Rewards loyalty program and co-branded credit-card business. CEO Bob Jordan has said Southwest does not need a long-haul network comparable with those of Delta Air Lines (DAL.N) , United Airlines (UAL.O) or American Airlines (AAL.O) . In May, he said 8 to 12 long-haul destinations could cover much of where Southwest customers want to travel. BOEING VERSUS AIRBUS Southwest currently operates an all-Boeing 737 fleet, but Airbus has been aggressively courting the airline as it evaluates future fleet needs, according to people familiar with the discussions. They said the A321XLR and A330neo could serve its long-haul needs, while the smaller A220 has been pitched for other parts of its network. Choosing Airbus would require Southwest to diversify its fleet. Those people said the 787 has appeared to hold the stronger position in the discussions. Southwest's pilot union has publicly indicated that more than one path is being examined. Jody Reven, president of the Southwest Airlines Pilots Association, said in a recent union podcast that the company had discussed both a "large aircraft" and a "narrow-body long-haul aircraft" as part of its future plans. AVAILABILITY COULD SHAPE TIMING The long-haul plan has been discussed on a roughly three-year timetable, one of the people said. But aircraft availability could shape the timing. Boeing has said the 787 is sold out through the end of the decade. One of the people said Southwest has explored obtaining some Dreamliners through lessors, potentially allowing an earlier launch. Another said aircraft from the secondary market had been considered for the initial fleet. Adding a 787 widebody would be a bigger undertaking than expanding Southwest's current 737 operation. Southwest has said adding a new aircraft type could require new maintenance and training programs, regulatory approvals and union negotiations over pay and work rules.

item.title: Simón se dirige a costa de México, tocará tierra como poderoso huracán
item.description: La tormenta tropical Simón se intensificaba rápidamente el jueves a medida que enfilaba hacia la costa occidental de México, donde tocará tierra como un "muy peligroso" huracán de categoría 4 el fin de semana, dijo el Centro Nacional de Huracanes (NHC, por su siglas en inglés) de Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La tormenta tropical Simón se intensificaba rápidamente el jueves a medida que enfilaba hacia la costa occidental de México, donde tocará tierra como un "muy peligroso" huracán de categoría 4 el fin de semana, dijo el Centro Nacional de Huracanes (NHC, por su siglas en inglés) de Estados Unidos. A las 14.00 hora local (2000 GMT) Simón, que estaba a punto de convertirse en un huracán de categoría 1 en la escala de Saffir-Simpson, se ubicaba a 370 kilómetros al sur de la ciudad portuaria Manzanillo y soplaba vientos máximos sostenidos de 110 kilómetros por hora (km/h), con ráfagas más fuertes, mientras se desplazaba hacia el oeste a 9 km/h, dijo el NHC. "Simón casi es un huracán", advirtió el NHC, con sede en Miami. "Se pronostica un fortalecimiento rápido, y se espera que Simón se convierta en huracán esta noche y en un huracán de categoría 4, muy peligroso, antes de llegar a la costa de México", agregó. Simón tocará tierra muy cerca de Manzanillo, el mayor puerto de México y principal puerta de entrada del comercio con Asia. El domingo, seguirá avanzando tierra adentro y pasará por Puerto Vallarta, un popular destino de playa cuyo municipio homónimo alberga a casi 300,000 habitantes. Un huracán de categoría 4, sopla vientos destructivos de hasta 250 km/h, descarga lluvias torrenciales y marejadas ciclónicas peligrosas. Además, puede dejar a su paso daños generalizados en estructuras protectoras, desplome de tejados en edificios pequeños e inundaciones en terrenos interiores. "La amenaza de huracán para el oeste de México está aumentando", dijo Tyler Roys, meteorólogo de AccuWeather, la compañía estadounidense que presta servicios comerciales de pronóstico del tiempo. "Algunas de las mismas zonas que sufrieron fuertes lluvias, vientos intensos y oleaje peligroso a causa del huracán Polo ahora se enfrentan a otra amenaza tropical", agregó. La semana pasada, [USN:L6N45L0YK TEXT:"Polo tocó tierra"] como un huracán de categoría 2 en la Península de Baja California dejando árboles y postes caídos, calles inundadas y otros daños materiales. Simon también podría llevar humedad tropical al suroeste de Estados Unidos la próxima semana. Se prevén precipitaciones de 25 a 50 milímetros (mm) en gran parte de Nuevo México, el este de Arizona, el sur de Colorado y el oeste de Texas, con la posibilidad de acumular de 50 a 100 mm en el sur de Nuevo México. Simon no será el único sistema tropical que afectará a México el domingo. Se pronostica que la tormenta tropical Rachel toque tierra en Baja California, provocando nuevos impactos tropicales en el país y el suroeste de Estados Unidos.

item.title: Flávio lidera 2º turno com 49% das intenções de voto contra 45% de Lula, diz Datafolha
item.description: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato do PL à Presidência, confirmou a liderança obtida no primeiro turno e saiu na frente na disputa do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, com 49% das intenções de voto contra 45% do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que tenta a reeleição, mostrou pesquisa Datafolha divulgada nesta quinta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato do PL à Presidência, confirmou a liderança obtida no primeiro turno e saiu na frente na disputa do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, com 49% das intenções de voto contra 45% do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que tenta a reeleição, mostrou pesquisa Datafolha divulgada nesta quinta-feira. Como a margem de erro da pesquisa é de 2 pontos percentuais, os dois candidatos estão no limite do empate técnico. Os indecisos somam apenas 1%, enquanto aqueles que dizem que votarão em branco, anularão o voto ou não votarão em nenhum candidato chegam a 5%. Em votos válidos, quando não são considerados os votos brancos e nulos e os indecisos, Flávio tem 52% contra 48% de Lula. No domingo, Flávio venceu o primeiro turno com 47,03% dos votos válidos, contra 45,16% de Lula. Segundo a pesquisa divulgada nesta quinta-feira, entre os eleitores que votaram em Augusto Cury (Avante), Renan Santos (Missão), Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) e Romeu Zema (Novo) no primeiro turno, a maioria declarou intenção de voto em Flávio agora. Conforme o Datafolha, 46% dos eleitores que votaram em Cury, Renan, Caiado e Zema disseram que votarão no candidato do PL no segundo turno. No mesmo universo de eleitores, 32% declararam voto em Lula agora.

item.title: US health secretary Kennedy launches new push on vaccine injuries
item.description: US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. this week launched an agency-wide effort to study and document any health problems reported after vaccination, the Department of Health and Human Services said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Aboulenein
item.content:encoded: US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. this week launched an agency-wide effort to study and document any health problems reported after vaccination, the Department of Health and Human Services said on Thursday. The initiative is the latest step by Kennedy, who spent years questioning vaccine safety and founded an anti-vaccine group before taking office, to reshape federal immunization policy. The American Academy of Pediatrics says childhood vaccines are studied in placebo-controlled and comparison-group trials and monitored for safety after approval. The federal Vaccine Injury Table lists 14 compensable injuries across 16 vaccine types under the Vaccine Injury Compensation Program, a no-fault system in which claimants file against the government, not vaccine makers. Since 1988, it has awarded roughly $5 billion across about 12,300 injury and death claims. The new moves, which appear to be part of Kennedy's decades-long efforts to sow skepticism about vaccines, come as he faces legal challenges to his attempts to alter US childhood vaccination schedules and growing concern among public health experts about falling immunization rates, particularly against measles, which has seen a resurgence in the US since last year. The effort centers on a National Institutes of Health clinic opened on Monday to treat and study patients reporting health problems after receiving vaccines, HHS said in a statement. Other measures include a proposal by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to reimburse physicians for reporting suspected injuries to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System, or VAERS; a CDC effort to update VAERS; and HHS requiring electronic health records to capture vaccine-related adverse events. Kennedy has said US children receive too many vaccines, falsely claiming repeatedly that kids get up to 90 doses before age 18, which has been echoed by President Donald Trump . Kennedy has long argued that chemicals in vaccines are dangerous, though experts say there is no evidence of harm. In his first year heading HHS, he [USN:L4N3SC1BC TEXT:"fired all 17 independent expert members"] of the CDC's vaccine advisory committee and selected new panelists, many of whom shared his anti-vaccine views. In January, the CDC announced a revamped childhood vaccine schedule that reduced recommended vaccines, dropping universal recommendations for flu, rotavirus, hepatitis A, hepatitis B at birth, some forms of meningitis and respiratory syncytial virus. A federal court issued [USN:L1N3ZF00J TEXT:"a preliminary injunction"] in March blocking key parts of the proposed changes, finding that Kennedy and HHS had violated federal law in reshaping the CDC's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices. The injunction has prevented ACIP from holding meetings to make recommendations on immunizations often needed for insurance coverage.
