Flávio disse mais cedo nesta quinta que o mecanismo de "split payment" introduzido pela reforma tributária sobre o consumo deverá produzir uma “quebradeira generalizada” de empresas, argumentando que, por isso, sua equipe estuda propor a [USN:L1N45U0K8 TEXT:"retirada"] desse sistema. Com o "split payment", tributos sobre o consumo serão automaticamente transferidos ao governo no momento da transação, em vez de serem recolhidos posteriormente pelas empresas, o que, para Flávio, prejudica o fluxo de caixa das companhias.

item.title: Big Ten commish: Sticking with '18 strong members' for now
item.description: Commissioner Tony Petitti sees no reason to make the Big Ten any bigger right now.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Commissioner Tony Petitti sees no reason to make the Big Ten any bigger right now. Petitti said Thursday at Big Ten basketball media days in Chicago there are no active talks or plans regarding expansion of the conference as rumors swirl about interest from LSU and Miami, among others. There are "absolutely no discussions taking place around expansion," Petitti said, with his explicit focus on helping current conference membership adjust to the evolving college landscape. "This conference has got 18 strong members," Petitti said. "We're focused on that. There's lots of things that we think we can do inside the conference to continue to grow the position that we have with the 18 members." The conference expanded most recently in 2024, plucking Pac-12 powers Oregon, UCLA, Southern California and Washington. Petitti said the Big Ten was supportive of the Protect College Sports Act, which provides a path toward helping conferences be in lockstep on wide-reaching realms such as eligibility limits, transfer rules and universal state adherence to existing legislation. "The bill isn't going to stop every possible thing," he said. "That's not what it's intended to do. In areas like eligibility, transfer, legislating litigation around NIL, states trying to come over the top of the system, and the settlement, this will clean all that up, and so that's really critical." --Michigan State head coach Tom Izzo knows all about the challenges of winning in the Big Ten, which houses 2026 Final Four teams and a heavily remodeled national champion in Ann Arbor. Michigan had three first-round NBA draft picks and head coach Dusty May "got drafted first," as Boynton put it Thursday, after cutting down the nets in Indianapolis. That Final Four also included Illinois. The Illini start the season with several new faces, too. Top freshman Keaton Wagler was a lottery pick of the Los Angeles Clippers. Izzo said he's been around long enough to know it's not the names and the faces but the places that will matter once conference play begins. "The Big Ten is going to be damn good. Michigan, Illinois, UCLA and USC have a lot of talent," he said. "I'm leaving others out. I think Maryland will be far improved. But what isn't appreciated is our home buildings. Every game is an event. You can't rest in this league." Michigan will be in the hands of Mike Boynton Jr., who replaced May upon his departure for the Dallas Mavericks. Not everything is new for the Wolverines. Guards Elliot Cadeau and Trey McKenney lead the cast of familiar faces hoping to put the defending champions in position to play in Detroit -- site of the 2027 Final Four -- at season's end. Boynton, an assistant under May, said his former boss is "the best I've ever been around just in terms of emotional IQ." "His ability to surround himself with high-quality, competent people and give them the vision to execute. The biggest part I've tried to replicate," Boynton said, "is just having the right people in the room." -- Less than 48 hours before Thursday's media-day appearance, Tony Stubblefield was an assistant on Dana Altman's Oregon staff. Suddenly, Stubblefield was thrust into the spotlight at Big Ten media days as the interim head coach at Oregon following Altman's retirement announcement Wednesday. That doesn't mean Altman's decision -- or its timing -- took Stubblefield by surprise. "Not totally surprised," Stubblefield said. "We had a challenging year last year... I think that took a lot out of him." Stubblefield was the head coach at DePaul from 2021-24, bookended by stints on the Ducks' staff. He was familiar with Eugene as far back as 2010. Stubblefield inherits a program that reached the NCAA Tournament's second round in 2024 and 2025 but missed the event in three of the past five seasons. Last season was Oregon's first sub-.500 finish under Altman (12-20). "Obviously it's a lot for these young men," Stubblefield said on Big Ten Network. "They came there to play for Dana Altman, to play at the University of Oregon. What I told them, we've got to stay more connected now. We've got to be tight. ... This is a very good group. We've had very good leadership with (seniors) Sean Stewart, Fred Payne, Andrew Meadow. And I told those guys we've gotta be tighter than ever." -- Rutgers also faces a coaching transition, with longtime head coach Steve Pikiell undergoing cancer treatment and associate head coach Brandin Knight temporarily directing the program. Knight represented the Scarlet Knights in Chicago and said the longtime head coach was guiding him from the background. "He's involved in my day-to-day, and I'm always checking on him from a standpoint of what he sees, what he's thinking, what I should be worried or concerned about," said Knight, who has never served as a head coach. "And then he takes some of the pressure off of myself just because he's still trying to be there as much as he can at every waking moment. "So at times we have to tell him -- yesterday he apologized to the staff for not being there for us and being able to do more. And it's just kind of a testament to who he is as a person and just as a supporter of us." --Michigan was far from the only Big Ten success story last March and April. The league had more participants in the Final Four (two), Elite Eight (four) and Sweet 16 (six) than any other conference. Ninth-seeded Iowa bested fourth-seeded Nebraska in a Sweet 16 Battle of the Corn. The Hawkeyes' reward under then-first-year coach Ben McCollum was to go up against a veteran Illinois team in the Elite Eight, and Brad Underwood guided the Fighting Illini to their first Final Four since 2005. Illinois returns several key contributors, bringing heightened expectations that Underwood believes his team should embrace. "(We're) not running from it. We're accepting the fact that people think we're pretty good, OK?" Underwood said. "We worked for that, we deserve that. Handle the ups and the downs. ... "This group hasn't done anything. Last year's team did. Keaton Wagler's not coming back through the door... Let's make our own identity, and let's make it a better one. The only way we know to do that is work." For the first time in a long time, McCollum will be without point guard Bennett Stirtz, whom he coached from Division II Northwest Missouri State to Drake to Iowa. The coach told Big Ten Network he'd need a by-committee approach to replace the do-everything Stirtz, who's now in the NBA. "I do think we'll play more players," he said. "I think you have to be careful with that, though, that you don't just play guys because you have them. You need to just play harder," McCollum said. --Field Level Media

item.title: Venezuela's president expects third-quarter growth after earthquake hit
item.description: Venezuela's economy is projected to expand 6.5% in the third quarter this year, acting President Delcy Rodriguez said on Thursday, highlighting recovery in both oil and non-oil sectors after devastating twin earthquakes struck the country in June.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Venezuela's economy is projected to expand 6.5% in the third quarter this year, acting President Delcy Rodriguez said on Thursday, highlighting recovery in both oil and non-oil sectors after devastating twin earthquakes struck the country in June. Oil production in the country increased 8% year-to-date, she added, speaking at an event with business leaders. Since the US capture of former President Nicolas Maduro in January, Washington has been trying to secure a stable flow of Venezuelan crude for US refineries while promoting American investment into the OPEC country's deteriorated energy industry. Venezuela currently produces some 1.25 million barrels per day of crude. Rodriguez added that the country expects to receive $12 billion in public and private financing over the next two years.

item.title: Taylor Farms suspenderá cosecha de lechuga en México durante temporadas de ciclosporiasis
item.description: Taylor Farms anunció el jueves que suspenderá indefinidamente la recolección y el procesamiento de lechuga iceberg procedente del centro de México destinada a la venta en Estados Unidos o Canadá durante la temporada de ciclosporiasis, tras un reciente brote que afectó a miles de personas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Taylor Farms anunció el jueves que suspenderá indefinidamente la recolección y el procesamiento de lechuga iceberg procedente del centro de México destinada a la venta en Estados Unidos o Canadá durante la temporada de ciclosporiasis, tras un reciente brote que afectó a miles de personas. El proveedor de productos frescos dijo que dejaría de comercializar lechuga iceberg de la región durante el periodo identificado por los Centros para el Control y la Prevención de Enfermedades (CDC) de Estados Unidos como la temporada de ciclosporiasis, que coincide con la época de lluvias en el centro de México. La temporada de ciclosporiasis en Estados Unidos se extiende del 1 de mayo al 31 de agosto, según la página web de los CDC. Más tarde, la empresa afirmó que espera satisfacer la demanda de lechuga iceberg con los cultivos que tienen tanto en Canadá como en Estados Unidos, sin dar más detalles. El brote de julio provocó que miles de personas enfermaran en todo Estados Unidos y alteró el funcionamiento de restaurantes, entre ellos los de Taco Bell, de Yum Brands (YUM.N) , que usaban la lechuga retirada del mercado. La contaminación provocó una de las mayores retiradas de productos alimenticios de los últimos años y reavivó el escrutinio de los controles de seguridad alimentaria de los productos agrícolas importados. La ciclosporiasis es una enfermedad intestinal causada por el parásito Cyclospora. Las personas pueden infectarse tras ingerir alimentos o agua contaminados, y los síntomas pueden incluir diarrea, calambres estomacales, náuseas y fatiga.

item.title: Fed's Musalem says tighter monetary policy needed to lower inflation
item.description: St. Louis Federal Reserve President Alberto Musalem said on Thursday the US central bank will need to hike interest rates again to bring inflation back to its 2% target, although he declined to say what policymakers should do at their meeting later this month.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: St. Louis Federal Reserve President Alberto Musalem said on Thursday the US central bank will need to hike interest rates again to bring [USN:L1N45M0L0 TEXT:"inflation back"] to its 2% target, although he declined to say what policymakers should do at their meeting later this month. "To bring inflation back to target in a timely manner, more monetary policy firming will be required," Musalem said at an event held by Bloomberg in New York. "If a timely manner is something like 18 months, that kind of suggests that rates ought to be going up further in an appropriate period of time in the next six to nine months," he said. Musalem, who is not a voting member of the central bank's rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee this year, demurred when asked if the Fed should raise rates at the October 27-28 meeting. "I go into every meeting with a very open mind, and I haven't prejudged what the outcome of that meeting is going to be, or what I'm going to do at that meeting," Musalem said, adding that the general direction of "inflation requires us to be thinking of further policy firming here." Traders broadly expect the Fed will hold its policy rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range at the meeting in October. The Fed [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"hiked rates"] at its September 15-16 meeting in an effort to bring high levels of inflation back to its target. Policymakers at that meeting also penciled in another rate hike by the end of this year. Traders had been putting strong odds on an October rate hike until New York Fed President John Williams said last week that there is [USN:S0N44V01O TEXT:"no urgency to act"] while the Fed weighs incoming data. Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson followed up by saying he saw no imminent need to raise rates. The Fed is now expected to deliver its next rate hike in December. 'UNSUSTAINABLE FISCAL PATH' In his remarks, Musalem said inflation is the economy's primary problem amid strong growth and a stable job market. He said the Fed can likely lower inflation without denting hiring, and that getting inflation back to the 2% goal would be broadly helpful. Musalem also noted that even with the notable rise in bond yields, "financial conditions remain accommodative and supportive of economic growth." He said the rise in yields does not signal investors are losing confidence in the Fed. Instead, yields are up on expectations that real rates will go up in a strong economy marked by a lot of competition for capital. Strong investment in the tech sector and large government borrowing needs are helping to keep yields up, he said. "The US federal government has been on an unsustainable fiscal path now for the better part of two decades," Musalem said, adding that "the risk is there" that heavy levels of government borrowing could create [USN:L6N45T16X TEXT:"problems"] for the economy.

item.title: Rosa prevê superávit comercial de ao menos US$90 bi em 2026, acima de estimativa oficial
item.description: O Brasil deve ter um superávit comercial de ao menos US$90 bilhões este ano a despeito da recente redução da estimativa oficial do governo para um saldo de cerca de US$85 bilhões, disse nesta quinta-feira o ministro de Indústria Comércio Bens e Serviços, Márcio Elias Rosa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Brasil deve ter um superávit comercial de ao menos US$90 bilhões este ano a despeito da recente redução da estimativa oficial do governo para um saldo de cerca de US$85 bilhões, disse nesta quinta-feira o ministro de Indústria Comércio Bens e Serviços, Márcio Elias Rosa. Segundo ele , o país vem apostando na diversificação de mercados para compensar o impacto sobre as exportações de movimentos como o tarifaço dos EUA e o embargo a carnes bovinas e de aves imposto pela União Europeia. “Continuo apostando em US$90 bilhões, se não passar de US$90 bilhões", disse ele a jornalistas na Firjan (Federação das Indústrias do Estado do Rio de Janeiro). Rosa disse que as negociações para flexibilização do tarifaço norte-americano estão caminhando e em três ou quatro semanas o governo brasileiro espera receber uma nova [USN:L1N45M15C TEXT:"proposta"] dos EUA. "Nós podemos constituir um grupo de trabalho, se for o caso, enquanto isso as equipes técnicas podem dialogar." O Mdic reduziu na terça-feira sua projeção para o superávit da balança comercial brasileira em 2026 a US$84,4 bilhões, contra previsão feita em julho de saldo de US$90 bilhões, prevendo ganho menor nas exportações e arrefecimento de preços internacionais. Apesar da revisão para baixo, o resultado ainda seria 24% mais forte do que o observado no ano anterior, quando o saldo foi de US$68,1 bilhões, e marcaria o segundo maior saldo da série histórica, atrás apenas do dado de 2023.

item.title: Law firms give lawyers time off billing grind to test-drive AI
item.description: (Billable Hours is Reuters' weekly report on lawyers and money. Please send tips or suggestions to D.Thomas@thomsonreuters.com)
item.dc:creator: Sara Merken, David Thomas
item.content:encoded: (Billable Hours is Reuters' weekly report on lawyers and money. Please send tips or suggestions to D.Thomas@thomsonreuters.com ) As Ropes & Gray ramps up its use of AI, the law firm said its 1,000-plus associates and counsel can now count up to 100 hours of AI experimenting and training toward their annual billing requirements. The move, part of a firmwide AI training initiative in place since the spring, expands on the firm's decision last year to allow first-year associates to [USN:L1N3WF0V8 TEXT:"devote up to 20% of their required billable hours"] – nearly 400 hours – to AI training and simulations. All of Boston-founded Ropes' first-year associates participated in the program, which the firm found to be a "huge success," said Patrick Ryan, its director of knowledge management innovation. A Ropes spokesperson said the firm has "invested over 35,000 associate hours to AI time this year" under the hourly-credit program. Law firms use hourly requirements to ensure lawyers are busy, assess their productivity and allocate bonuses. Devoting a portion of them to non-client work is another sign of the legal industry's investment in AI, which firms are using to speed up legal work and streamline their business operations. Two Ropes associates told Reuters the credit program gives them flexibility to try AI tools even when it can't be billed directly to clients. Kevin Schoonveld, a New York-based ninth-year debt finance associate, said learning to use prompts that yield accurate results takes time that busy associates might otherwise be less willing to commit. “When you're first playing around with these AI tools, you're investing a lot of time in it and you're not seeing a ton of efficiencies at first," he said. Some other firms are also allowing limited billable hours credits for work using AI that’s not directly for clients. At Akerman, lawyers since April have been able to get credit for AI-related projects that are “really contributing value” to the firm, said chairman Scott Meyers. He said the firm posts AI assignments on an internal portal for associates to take up or propose their own. So far, associate projects have included building an AI agent to review construction contracts and testing AI research tools to document where they have produced inaccurate results, he said. “We understand that there may be some compression in billable hours” due to AI being able to handle more work, Meyers said. But he said that alone shouldn't dictate a need for fewer associates, and the credits program helps to address associates' concerns about AI's impact on the time they're billing. “If we need to find other ways to fill that time, I suspect it will be that combination of billable and creditable hours,” he said. As at most large firms, billable hours credits are also allocated for pro bono work. At Ropes & Gray, the AI credits are part of a broader training and professional development program for all the firm's attorneys. Lawyers move through training modules toward applying AI to client work and are later encouraged to develop internal AI tools or processes, Ryan said. The firm is also including AI as a topic in lawyers' annual review conversations, but not with the aim of penalizing them, said Amy Ross, the firm's chief legal talent officer. "To the extent that we're finding people aren't using it, we want to address that too," she said. KIRKLAND TIGHTENS LID ON FINANCES Kirkland & Ellis, the highest-grossing US law firm, said it will no longer report its annual financial results to The American Lawyer. The firm, whose revenue topped $10 billion last year, said in a Wednesday letter to editors at the legal trade publication that "public reporting of our revenue and profits does not provide meaningful value to our clients nor adequately reflect the caliber of our firm’s legal services." It said publicizing its finances for ranking purposes "could incentivize quantitative metrics over qualitative strengths," like the quality of its legal services, according to the letter, which was viewed by Reuters. The American Lawyer annually publishes lists of the 200 highest-grossing and most profitable law firms in the country. Kirkland, driven in part by its private equity and restructuring work, has topped the revenue rankings since 2017. Kirkland's revenue hit $10.56 billion in 2025, while its average profits per equity partner reached $11.1 million. The firm has a tiered partnership in which a substantial number of partners do not have a traditional ownership stake. Also on Billable Hours' radar this week... --AT&T's legal department has stopped paying law firms to handle many routine assignments typically done by junior lawyers, and is instead using an in-house team using AI, Reuters columnist Sara Randazzo [USN:L6N45S1A5 TEXT:"reports"]. AT&T's general counsel said its roster of 30 or so outside law firms could shrink in the future. --President Donald Trump’s administration is vying in federal court to allow the EEOC to keep information secret from the public about its probes last year targeting the employment practices at some major US law firms. The [USN:L6N45S09L TEXT:"administration is contesting"] a lawsuit over access to the records and says a significant amount of information must remain confidential. --Cornell University has [USN:L6N45S15B TEXT:"hired Sally Yates"], who served as deputy US attorney general from 2015 to 2017, for an internal investigation of how it handled a student's allegations that she was gang-raped, a case that has brought mounting scrutiny and triggered student protests at the Ivy League school. Read more: [USN:L6N45K07C TEXT:"Thousands of web-tracking lawsuits face extinction under California overhaul"] [USN:L6N45D0X6 TEXT:"Law firms vie for tech talent in AI race"] [USN:L6N42308A TEXT:"AI error-ridden court filings surge despite three years of sanctions"]

item.title: Hurricane Isaias strengthens as US Gulf Coast prepares for landfall
item.description: Hurricane Isaias strengthened on Thursday as it barreled toward the US Gulf Coast, prompting mandatory evacuations in parts of Florida and emergency declarations in Alabama as forecasters warned of life-threatening storm surges, tornadoes and flooding.
item.dc:creator: Brad Brooks
item.content:encoded: Hurricane Isaias strengthened on Thursday as it barreled toward the US Gulf Coast, prompting mandatory evacuations in parts of Florida and emergency declarations in Alabama as forecasters warned of life-threatening storm surges, tornadoes and flooding. Isaias has already severely disrupted oil and gas production in the Gulf of Mexico, forcing energy companies to evacuate offshore platforms and shut down operations. The first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season was packing maximum sustained winds of 85 mph (140 kph) early on Thursday, the US National Hurricane Center said. Isaias was forecast to strengthen to near Category 3 intensity, with sustained winds reaching 110 mph (175 kph) on Friday before reaching the northern Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday. "We are expecting Isaias to be a dangerous hurricane when it makes landfall,” NHC director Michael Brennan said in a Thursday morning briefing. "Today is the day to prepare and get ready." Isaias nearly tied the record for the latest first Atlantic hurricane with one that hit on October 8, 1905. The strong El Nino weather pattern this year has suppressed Atlantic hurricane development by increasing vertical wind shear, which disrupts the formation of strengthening tropical storms. The hurricane was moving east-northeast at 10 mph (17 kph), about 355 miles (570 km) south of the mouth of the Mississippi River at 1 p.m. US Central time, the NHC said. IMPACTS ON OIL, GAS The Marine Minerals Administration, which monitors offshore US oil and gas operators in the Gulf of Mexico, said on Thursday that personnel have been evacuated from 121 production platforms and five non-dynamically positioned rigs ahead of the storm. About 63% of current oil production in the Gulf, or 1.3 million barrels of oil a day, has been shut in, the agency said, citing operator reports. Just over 1.1 billion cubic feet a day of natural gas production has also been shut in, or about 57% of total output from the region. On Wednesday, 25% of oil production and 16% of natural gas output had been shut in. About 9 million barrels of oil production could be lost across the Gulf through the duration of the storm, a marked increase from the 7.1 million barrels impacted by Tropical Storm Bertha in July, according to a model forecast from consulting firm Earth Science Associates. The companies with the most exposure to the storm include BP, Chevron (CVX.N) , ENI, Murphy Oil (MUR.N) and Shell (SHEL.L) , among others, according to the Earth Science model. WARNINGS, STORM SURGE Hurricane warnings stretched from coastal Mississippi through Alabama to the Florida panhandle, while tropical-storm and storm-surge warnings extended into southeastern Louisiana, the NHC said. Forecasters warned that storm surges could reach 5 to 7 feet (1.5 to 2.1 meters) above sea level in the hardest-hit coastal areas, with rainfall of 3 to 7 inches (8 to 18 cm) and isolated totals of 15 inches (38 cm). The hurricane was forecast to weaken somewhat as it approached land. Increasing vertical wind shear, which can disrupt a hurricane's circulation, was expected to limit its strength near landfall, though forecasters warned it would remain dangerous. EVACUATIONS ORDERED In Florida, officials ordered mandatory evacuations beginning at noon local time on Thursday for coastal areas of Okaloosa County. The county urged tourists to leave the area and announced plans to close three airports Thursday evening. Governor Ron DeSantis declared a state of emergency in 25 Florida counties earlier in the week. Alabama Governor Kay Ivey declared a state of emergency covering 40 counties, while officials on Dauphin Island issued an evacuation notice for the western portion of the barrier island beginning Thursday evening. Baldwin County, Alabama, encouraged residents of low-lying coastal areas to evacuate voluntarily and prepared emergency shelters. In Mississippi, Jackson County and the city of Gautier declared local emergencies as coastal communities prepared for flooding and power outages.

item.title: Precios de bonos Tesoro EEUU cambian de tendencia y suben tras subasta de deuda a 30 años
item.description: Los precios de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos subieron el jueves, y la mayoría de los retornos descendió por segunda vez en la semana, después de que una sólida demanda en una subasta a 30 años sugiriera que los inversores siguen dispuestos a comprar deuda pública a largo plazo pese a una reciente ola de ventas.
item.dc:creator: Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss
item.content:encoded: Los precios de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos subieron el jueves, y la mayoría de los retornos descendió por segunda vez en la semana, después de que una sólida demanda en una subasta a 30 años sugiriera que los inversores siguen dispuestos a comprar deuda pública a largo plazo pese a una reciente ola de ventas. * Más temprano en la sesión, los bonos se vieron presionados por el alza de los precios del petróleo. El crudo retrocedió ligeramente después de que el presidente Donald Trump afirmara que Estados Unidos no lanzaría un ataque contra Irán antes de las elecciones legislativas de mitad de mandato de noviembre. * En las operaciones de la tarde, el rendimiento de referencia a 10 años cayó 5 puntos básicos, al 5,227%, tras haber alcanzado el miércoles su nivel más alto en 24 años. * Los retornos a 30 años cedieron 5,9 puntos básicos, al 5,602%. La caída de los rendimientos implica un aumento en el precio de los bonos del Tesoro. * En el tramo corto de la curva, la rentabilidad a dos años, que refleja las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés, bajó 1,3 puntos básicos, al 4,751% . * Los analistas señalaron que el éxito de la subasta a 30 años fue un factor clave para el repunte. El bono se colocó con un rendimiento del 5,618%, por debajo de la tasa esperada justo antes de la subasta, lo que indica que los inversores compraron el título sin exigir una mayor rentabilidad. * La ratio de cobertura, una medida de la demanda, también fue elevada, situándose en 2,54 veces, frente a un promedio de 2,41 veces en las seis subastas previas. Las ofertas indirectas, que incluyen a inversores extranjeros, absorbieron el 72,3% de la emisión, superando el promedio del 69,1% registrada en las seis operaciones previas. * No obstante, el petróleo sigue siendo un factor determinante para los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro, ya que aviva la preocupación por la inflación. * Los futuros del Brent cerraron en 104,28 dólares por barril, con un alza del 4,07%, mientras que los futuros del crudo estadounidense ganaron un 3,65%, a 91,49 dólares. * Ambos contratos llegaron a escalar más de 5 dólares por barril durante la sesión, impulsados por la persistente inquietud sobre el suministro de petróleo en Oriente Medio tras los ataques a buques en el Golfo y el estrecho de Ormuz.

item.title: Russia's Yandex says it is unclear whether data centre can be restored after drone strike
item.description: Russian technology and AI company Yandex said on Thursday it could not yet determine whether equipment at a data centre hit by a Ukrainian drone attack could be restored.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian technology and AI company Yandex said on Thursday it could not yet determine whether equipment at a data centre hit by a Ukrainian drone attack could be restored. Yandex [USN:L1N45U04H TEXT:"said"] earlier that the attack on its Sasovo hub, one of its five large data centres, caused a fire and forced it to suspend operations at the site, which hosts tens of thousands of servers. "The scale of the damage to the infrastructure is still being assessed," Yandex said in a statement. "For the moment, we cannot confirm whether it is possible to restore the data centre equipment in Sasovo." The company earlier said some of its services were unavailable and specialist teams were at the site assessing the damage. Two of Yandex's three supercomputers, used to develop its AI model, are housed at the Sasovo data centre. Yandex has not said whether they were damaged. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, speaking to reporters in Kyiv, did not refer specifically to the strike on Yandex, but said Ukraine was "mirroring" Russian attacks on data centres. "We always respond in mirror-like fashion," [USN:L1N45U0TV TEXT:"Zelenskiy said"]. "You all know, they have been hitting and continue to hit our data centres. We are responding. I can't share all the details."

item.title: US bonds rally after 30-year auction finds solid demand
item.description: US Treasuries rose on Thursday, with most yields across the curve falling for just the second time this week, after a 30-year bond auction met with solid demand, showing investors remain willing to buy long-dated government debt, despite the ongoing market selloff.
item.dc:creator: Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss
item.content:encoded: US Treasuries rose on Thursday, with most yields across the curve falling for just the second time this week, after a 30-year bond auction met with solid demand, showing investors remain willing to buy long-dated government debt, despite the ongoing market selloff. Earlier in the session, Treasuries were pressured by higher oil prices. Crude oil pulled back slightly after President Donald Trump said that the [USN:L1N45U0PH TEXT:"US will not launch an attack"] on Iran before midterm elections in November. In afternoon trading, the benchmark 10-year yield was down 5 basis points to 5.227% after hitting a 24-year high on Wednesday. US 30-year yields also declined, down 5.9 bps at 5.602% . When Treasury prices fall, yields rise. On the shorter end of the curve, US 2-year yields, which reflect interest rate expectations, dipped 1.3 bps to 4.751% . Analysts said the strong 30-year auction was a big factor for the rally. The issue priced at a yield of [USN:AQN2MNC9C TEXT:"5.618%"], below the expected rate at the bid deadline, which meant investors bought the bond without demanding higher compensation. The bid-to-cover ratio, a measure of demand, was also high at 2.54, better than the average of 2.41 times over the last six auctions. Indirect bids, which include foreign investors, took 72.3% of supply, up from an average of 69.1% over the last six auctions. Jay Hatfield, chief executive officer at Infrastructure Capital Management, said he thinks 10-year Treasury yields have peaked. "The peak was probably the 5.30% level, maybe even lower and we believe we have already seen peak pessimism about Fed rate increases," Hatfield said. He believes the Fed will only be able to raise interest rates just once in this cycle, as opposed to the three currently being factored in by the market. "We think the Fed's being irrational by all this tough talk on inflation," Hatfield said. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said on Thursday [USN:L6N45T15S TEXT:"additional rate hikes"] will likely be needed to lower inflation to the Fed's 2% target, but added there was "flexibility" about the pace of increases. His comments pushed 2-year yields higher, which rose faster than 10-year yields. The yield curve flattened on Thursday, with the spread between 2-year and 10-year yields narrowing to 47.1 bps from 51.4 bps. Earlier in the session, the curve hit 54.2 bps, steepest since mid-August. OIL AS MAJOR DRIVER Oil remains a major driver of Treasury yields, stoking inflation concerns. Brent crude settled at $103.92 per barrel, up 3.7%, while US crude futures ended 3.4% higher at $91.17. Both contracts at one point were up $5 a barrel on [USN:L1N45U031 TEXT:"persistent worries"] about oil supply in the Middle East . "The market remains content to trade the energy shock solely from the perspective of the inflationary implications, largely ignoring any potential demand destruction that could follow," wrote Ian Lyngen, head of US rates strategy at BMO, in a research note.

item.title: EEUU congela programa de visas a Microsoft y otras tecnológicas; investiga universidades
item.description: Estados Unidos suspendió el jueves a Microsoft , a las principales empresas de externalización de tecnologías de información y al fabricante de software Adobe de un programa de visas, e inició investigaciones a nueve universidades de prestigio.
item.dc:creator: Akash Sriram, Steve Holland
item.content:encoded: Estados Unidos suspendió el jueves a Microsoft (MSFT.O) , a las principales empresas de externalización de tecnologías de información y al fabricante de software Adobe (ADBE.O) de un programa de visas, e inició investigaciones a nueve universidades de prestigio. El Gobierno amplió de esta manera una campaña de represión que, dice, tiene como objetivo combatir el fraude y proteger los puestos de trabajo estadounidenses. Desde que asumió el cargo, el presidente Donald Trump ha llevado a cabo una extensa campaña para reducir el número de personas nacidas en el extranjero en Estados Unidos y restringir su acceso a la residencia y la ciudadanía. Las dos medidas adoptadas el jueves suponen el golpe más contundente hasta la fecha contra los programas de inmigración de trabajadores cualificados, lo que podría cortar una vía habitual hacia la residencia permanente para los trabajadores extranjeros del sector tecnológico, y ponen en la mira a algunas de las universidades de investigación más prestigiosas del país. "Lamentablemente, no ha habido ninguna empresa en Estados Unidos que haya abusado más del sistema que Microsoft", dijo el vicepresidente JD Vance. Vance señaló que la empresa despidió a 6.000 trabajadores estadounidenses el año pasado, al tiempo que se benefició de 6.300 visados de trabajador temporal H-1B y de casi 3 000 tarjetas de residencia. Los comentarios los hizo horas antes de un homenaje de Trump a varios multimillonarios del sector tecnológico por sus contribuciones a Estados Unidos, entre ellos el presidente ejecutivo de Microsoft, Satya Nadella. Nadella tuvo en su día un visado H-1B, al igual que Elon Musk, quien también fue homenajeado, lo mismo que otros tres presidentes ejecutivos inmigrantes. Microsoft es la empresa que más solicitudes PERM presenta, es decir, el proceso de certificación laboral permanente, según datos del Departamento de Trabajo. En el marco del PERM, que se exige para la mayoría de las tarjetas de residencia basadas en el empleo, las empresas deben demostrar que la contratación de personal extranjero no perjudicará los salarios ni los puestos de trabajo de los trabajadores estadounidenses. La empresa dijo en un comunicado que alrededor del 80% de las solicitudes de visado H-1B que presentó en el último ejercicio fiscal tenían como objetivo prorrogar o modificar la situación de los empleados actuales, y no contratar a nuevos trabajadores. En julio anunció que recortaría 4.800 puestos de trabajo, aproximadamente el 2,1% de su plantilla global.

item.title: Flávio promete reajustar aposentadoria acima da inflação
item.description: O senador e candidato à Presidência, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), prometeu nesta quinta-feira que, se eleito, reajustará os valores da aposentadoria acima da inflação e negou planos para mudar a forma atual de correção dos benefícios da Previdência e do Benefício de Prestação Continuada (BPC), após o jornal Folha de S. Paulo publicar mais cedo que sua equipe estuda alterar esses reajustes, assim como a correção dos gastos obrigatórios com saúde e educação.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O senador e candidato à Presidência, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), prometeu nesta quinta-feira que, se eleito, reajustará os valores da aposentadoria acima da inflação e negou planos para mudar a forma atual de correção dos benefícios da Previdência e do Benefício de Prestação Continuada (BPC), após o jornal Folha de S. Paulo publicar mais cedo que sua equipe estuda alterar esses reajustes, assim como a correção dos gastos obrigatórios com saúde e educação. Perguntado por jornalistas se reajustaria a aposentadoria acima da inflação, ele respondeu "sim", ao término de uma entrevista coletiva em Brasília para anunciar o apoio do Podemos à sua candidatura no segundo turno da eleição presidencial, onde enfrentará no dia 25 de outubro o presidente e candidato à reeleição Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). "Não caia nessa fake news do PT dizendo que eu vou acabar com o reajuste à aposentadoria. Pelo contrário, minha avó é professora aposentada do Estado. Eu sei da dificuldade que ela tem de fazer compra no final do mês, tenho que ajudar ela de vez em quando, meus irmãos têm que ajudar a minha avó e meu avô de vez em quando, porque os dois são aposentados", disse Flávio. O senador afirmou que o ajuste fiscal que seu eventual governo fará se concentrará em outras despesas que não os benefícios sociais. Mais cedo, após a publicação da reportagem da Folha de S. Paulo, o economista [USN:L6N45U0SH TEXT:"Adolfo Sachsida"], um dos coordenadores da área econômica da campanha de Flávio, afirmou que, se o senador for eleito presidente, o próximo governo irá fortalecer programas sociais e reduzir impostos. Sachsida negou que o candidato planeje privatizar estatais como Petrobras, Banco do Brasil e Caixa Econômica Federal. Após Flávio terminar o primeiro turno da eleição, disputado no último domingo, cerca de 2,2 milhões de votos à frente de Lula, o Ibovespa, índice de referência do mercado de ações brasileiro, teve um forte rali, ficando acima dos 200 mil pontos, e o dólar teve forte queda, chegando a operar abaixo de R$5. Boa parte dos agentes do mercado considera que, com Flávio no Planalto, crescem as chances de um maior controle das contas públicas -- ainda que o candidato não tenha apresentado propostas concretas de ajuste - o que abriria espaço para juros mais baixos e uma redução na trajetória de crescimento da dívida pública.

item.title: Latam prevê anunciar até quatro novos destinos com jatos Embraer em novembro
item.description: A Latam Brasil espera anunciar no final de novembro uma segunda fase da expansão de sua malha com aviões Embraer E195-E2 , incluindo até quatro novos destinos, afirmou nesta quinta-feira o presidente-executivo da companhia, Jerome Cadier.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Araujo
item.content:encoded: A Latam Brasil (LTM.SN) espera anunciar no final de novembro uma segunda fase da expansão de sua malha com aviões Embraer E195-E2 (EMBJ3.SA) , incluindo até quatro novos destinos, afirmou nesta quinta-feira o presidente-executivo da companhia, Jerome Cadier. Em evento na sede da fabricante em São José dos Campos (SP) para receber a primeira das 24 aeronaves encomendadas pela Latam, o executivo destacou que uma terceira leva de rotas deve ser divulgada no início do ano que vem. "Devemos anunciar a fase 2 no finalzinho de novembro, e a já devemos adicionar mais provavelmente três a quatro destinos. E em fevereiro do ano que vem já falar da fase 3, e aí sim completariam as 24 aeronaves", disse Cadier. A Latam anunciou em agosto a primeira fase da implementação dos E195-E2 em sua operação doméstica, com 14 jatos destinados a 42 rotas, incluindo oito novas ligações e quatro novas bases: Ji-Paraná (RO), Rondonópolis (TO), Cabo Frio (RJ) e Macaé (RJ). Os voos com o modelo começarão em novembro. Cadier lembrou que a expansão tem sido impulsionada por uma demanda robusta por viagens de negócios, chamando atenção para a "composição corporativa bastante grande" nos quatro novos destinos revelados em agosto. A decisão pelas rotas levou em conta áreas com forte demanda do setor agrícola, como Ji-Paraná e Rondonópolis, e da indústria petrolífera, como Macaé. "As outras que vêm pela frente também vão ter um mix entre turismo e corporativo, mas acho que é uma tônica do crescimento do mercado doméstico nos últimos anos ter sido um mercado resiliente do ponto de vista de viagens de negócios, e provavelmente vai continuar assim", afirmou o executivo. Cadier disse ainda que as novas rotas anunciadas em agosto têm apresentado desempenho positivo de vendas desde o lançamento. O executivo acrescentou que a Latam poderia eventualmente incluir rotas para outros países da América do Sul em suas operações com o E2. "É uma possibilidade. Não nessa fase 1 ou fase 2, mas talvez na fase 3, essas rotas que chamamos de regionais dentro da América do Sul", disse. A Latam possui um pedido firme de 24 aeronaves E195-E2 da Embraer, além de opções para adquirir outras 50 unidades. O presidente da Embraer, Francisco Gomes Neto, afirmou que a entrada da companhia na base de operadores do modelo reforça a relevância global da aeronave. "Não só no Brasil, para os brasileiros voarem mais de E2 por aqui, mas para o mundo todo passa uma mensagem de que esse avião é muito adequado para abrir novas rotas, oferecer maior frequência de voo. É muito importante para nós, a gente está muito contente com isso", disse.

item.title: Genre-defying Canadian poet Anne Carson wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
item.description: Canadian poet and writer Anne Carson, whose work often blends verse, prose, dialogue and translation in a genre-defying mix, won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature on Thursday for what the Swedish Academy called her "bold and inventive oeuvre".
item.dc:creator: Simon Johnson, Marie Mannes, Justyna Pawlak
item.content:encoded: Canadian poet and writer Anne Carson, whose work often blends verse, prose, dialogue and translation in a genre-defying mix, won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature on Thursday for what the Swedish Academy called her "bold and inventive oeuvre". "Crazy, I think they're all crazy," Carson told Icelandic broadcaster RUV when asked how she was feeling after learning she had won while on the Arctic island. "I'll get a sticker on the front of my book." Carson, 76, who was born in Toronto and has a home in Iceland, had been taken by surprise when called with the news, said Ingrid Carlberg, permanent secretary of the Academy, which awards the prize worth 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2 million). "All she had time to tell me was that she is for the moment in Iceland, where she's listening to the wind," Carlberg told a press conference in Stockholm after the announcement. She is widely known for her translations of classical Greek literature, which heavily influences her work that ranges from opera libretti to literary criticism and verse novels such as "Autobiography of Red" from 1998. "Genre is something for booksellers. It's something you do in order to appeal to an audience and make them buy books. And on what shelf do you put Anne Carson's books? It's on a shelf of her own," said Swedish novelist Steve Sem-Sandberg, who is a member of the award committee. "That's what I like about her." 'NEW FORMS OF CONTEMPORARY LITERATURE' In its citation, the Swedish Academy said it was recognising Carson "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature". "Almost all her literary production has centred upon the intersection between the philologist's obsession with words and the poet's desire for new meaning," the Academy said. "She has herself identified the etymology of words as the starting point for all her work. Her translations from Classical Greek may be regarded as independent works in their own right." Her style is exemplified in "Norma Jeane Baker of Troy" from 2019, a performance piece which mixes the stories of Helen of Troy in Euripides' play "Helen" with Marilyn Monroe. LIFE WITHOUT PROUST Often heralded as her greatest work, "Autobiography of Red" demonstrates Carson's ability to "actualise the classical literary tradition", the Academy said. In the book, she re-examines age-old questions such as "What happens when you love someone who will ultimately destroy you?" Tapping into more modern inspirations, Carson reflected on the character of Albertine, one of the narrator Marcel's love interests in Marcel Proust's "In Search of Lost Time", in her own book "The Albertine Workout". Carson had spent seven years reading Proust's masterpiece and said in an interview with Canada's CBC Radio One in 2016 that she suffered withdrawal symptoms after finishing, leading her to write "The Albertine Workout" as a way to prolong the experience. "You think life goes on after Proust, but it seems so grey," she said. BOXING LESSONS TO FIGHT PARKINSON'S Carson started taking boxing lessons when she was already in her 70s because of a Parkinson's disease diagnosis. The sport is recommended as a therapy because it helps with paying attention to hand-eye coordination and the sequencing of actions. She reflected on the disease's impact on her handwriting in an interview at the Louisiana Literary Festival in Denmark in 2024: "I scrub out whole paragraphs in shame ... the shame of bad handwriting." Carson, who has taught classics at universities in Canada and the United States, has said that she considers herself a visual artist as much as a literary one. "I think of making a poem as making an object. I have always thought of them more as drawings than as texts, but drawings that are also physically enterable through the fact of language," she said in the CBC interview. Poetry, she says, may be more attuned to the fast modern-day life than long-form writing. "I think it's probably more useful than prose right now because it's faster and everybody is in a hurry so basically it's good because it is brief," she told the Icelandic broadcaster on Thursday. When asked by the Nobel Committee about her own sources of inspiration, however, she listed ancient Greek poet Homer, author of "The Odyssey" epic. As to how the classical stories she has reinterpreted in her work might be relevant to modern audiences, she said: "I don't think I'm interested in relevance." 'AT HOME' IN ICELAND AND NYC Carson and her husband, artist Robert Currie, first came to Iceland after the 2008 banking collapse and gradually spent more time there. "We got to know people and we liked the people," Carson told Iceland Review in 2023. She has held citizenship of Iceland since 2022. Currie told the magazine Iceland was one of only two places that immediately felt like home to him, the other being New York City in the 1970s. Literature was the fourth of this year's Nobels to be announced this week, following [USN:L1N45R0AK TEXT:"medicine"], [USN:L1N45S0E6 TEXT:"physics"] and [USN:L1N45T09K TEXT:"chemistry"]. The peace prize winner will be announced in Oslo on Friday. Established in the will of Swedish dynamite inventor and businessman Alfred Nobel, the prizes have been awarded since 1901. Carson, who had been among the favourites this year, takes a place beside luminaries such as Alexander Solzhenitsyn, Alice Munro and Ernest Hemingway as a recipient of the award. Last year's prize was won by Hungarian writer [USN:L2N3VQ0DK TEXT:"Laszlo Krasznahorkai"]. ($1 = 10.0190 Swedish crowns)

item.title: Monedas cotizan mixtas en medio datos locales, peso México se hunde tras minutas Banxico
item.description: Las principales monedas de América Latina cotizaron dispares el jueves, tras datos de inflación locales, en una jornada en que el peso mexicano cayó con fuerza tras la divulgación de las minutas de la última reunión de Banco de México.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Farías
item.content:encoded: Las principales monedas de América Latina cotizaron dispares el jueves, tras datos de inflación locales, en una jornada en que el peso mexicano cayó con fuerza tras la divulgación de las minutas de la última reunión de Banco de México. * Las monedas de la región ya sentían cierta presión más temprano por una fuerte alza de los precios del petróleo, con el contrato Brent escalando más de 4 dólares y superando los 104 dólares el barril. * Eso respaldó al dólar en un principio, pero el billete verde retrocedió después de cotizar cerca de máximos de 18 meses, ante un descenso de los rendimientos de los bonos europeos. * El peso mexicano bajaba por la tarde un 1,26%, a 18,202 por dólar; en tanto que el índice S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) , integrado por las 35 acciones más líquidas del mercado, 0,49%, a 64.968,4 puntos, recuperándose en parte de la fuerte caía de la sesión previa. * Tres de los cinco miembros de la Junta de Gobierno del Banco de México señalaron que podrían considerarse futuros recortes de las tasas de interés si mejoran las perspectivas de inflación, revelaron las actas del encuentro de septiembre del banco central. * Eso contrasta con las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal podría aumentar el costo del crédito en su reunión de diciembre, haciendo más atractivo el invertir en activos estadounidenses. * Además, la [USN:L1N45U0FT TEXT:"inflación general"] de México se aceleró en septiembre, aunque menos de lo previsto, mientras que el índice subyacente continuó moderándose, afianzando las expectativas de que el banco central mantendría sin cambios la tasa clave de interés durante algún tiempo. * El real brasileño revirtió leves alzas previas y retrocedió un 0,17%, a 5,0240 unidades por dólar, al tiempo que el referencial bursátil Bovespa (.BVSP) escaló un 1,03%, a 206.402 puntos, respaldada por el avance de los papeles de Petrobras ante la escalada de los precios del crudo. * Los mercados brasileños aguardaban la primera encuesta electoral de Datafolha con miras al balotaje de finales de mes entre el senador de derecha Flávio Bolsonaro y el presidente de izquierda Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. * El peso chileno , cedió leves ganancias de primera hora y cerró la sesión con una caída del 0,1%, en 979,20/979,50 unidades por dólar, presionado por un importante retroceso en los precios del cobre, el mayor envío del país. En tanto, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) subió un 0,22%, a 11.024,22 puntos. * El cobre registró una fuerte caída el jueves cediendo las ganancias iniciales impulsadas por el regreso al mercado de China, el principal consumidor, ya que la subida vertiginosa de los precios del petróleo lastró las perspectivas de demanda de los metales industriales. * Mientras, los precios al consumidor en Chile subieron un 0,4% en septiembre, informó el Instituto Nacional de Estadísticas (INE), lo que estuvo ligeramente por debajo de una encuesta de Reuters a economistas que apuntaba a un aumento del 0,5%. En 12 meses la inflación [USN:L1N4500CR TEXT:"se mantuvo"] en 4,1%, por encima del rango de tolerancia del Banco Central de entre 2 y 4%. * El peso colombiano finalizó con ganancia de un 0,67% a 3.217,20 unidades por dólar, en su segunda sesión de apreciación. * En tanto, el índice accionario de la bolsa, el COLCAP (.COLCAP) , perdió un 0,37% a 2.525,90 puntos, después de que el Gobierno reportó que la inflación mantuvo su tendencia alcista en septiembre, lo que podría impulsar nuevos aumentos de la tasa de interés del Banco Central, favoreciendo la entrada de capitales externos hacia los mercados o "carry trade". * El peso argentino interbancario ganó un leve 0,07% a 1.517 por dólar , lejos de las bandas de intervención del banco central (BCRA), que mantuvo sus compras diarias para reforzar las reservas internacionales. La adquisición oficial del día sumó 43 millones de dólares. * El índice líder S&P Merval (.MERV) de la bolsa de Buenos Aires, en tanto, ganó un 0,3% después de ceder gran parte de sus avences que lo llevaron a escalar más de un 1% en la sesión. * "Argentina cotiza el riesgo de recesión mientras el Merval defiende su soporte", sintetizó Ion Jauregui, analista de ActivTrades. * Los mercados peruanos permanecieron cerrados por un feriado local.

item.title: Wall Street cae por el alza del crudo y la baja de las empresas de chips
item.description: Wall Street cerró en baja el jueves, en una jornada de alza de los precios del petróleo por el recrudecimiento de la tensión en Oriente Medio, a lo que se sumó un recorte de la producción estadounidense que avivó el temor a la inflación y una subida de las tasas de interés.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Culp, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: Wall Street cerró en baja el jueves, en una jornada de alza de los precios del petróleo por el recrudecimiento de la tensión en Oriente Medio, a lo que se sumó un recorte de la producción estadounidense que avivó el temor a la inflación y una subida de las tasas de interés. Las acciones del sector de los semiconductores se desplomaron. Los tres principales índices bursátiles estadounidenses perdieron terreno, y el Nasdaq, de gran peso tecnológico, fue el que más cayó. Los fabricantes de chips (.SOX) , que se han disparado más de un 80% en lo que va de año, fueron claramente los que peor se desempeñaron, con una caída del 3,0%. A los inversionistas les preocupa que la subida de las tasas pueda convertirse en un obstáculo para la rápida expansión de la inteligencia artificial, que se ha apoyado en gran medida en la deuda para su financiación. "El mercado se encuentra en un estado de nerviosismo debido a los altos precios del petróleo, mientras se prepara para la temporada de resultados, que básicamente comienza la semana que viene", dijo Peter Cardillo, economista jefe de mercado de Spartan Capital Securities. "Esa es la excusa para lo que, en mi opinión, es una toma de ganancias". El petróleo se disparó por la preocupación por la oferta tras una serie de ataques a buques en el estrecho de Ormuz, a lo que se sumó un recorte de la producción estadounidense debido a la actividad de los huracanes. La escasez mundial de petróleo durante la guerra de Irán ha provocado que el crudo estadounidense se haya disparado más de un 60% en el año, lo que ha avivado las presiones inflacionarias. Durante la sesión del jueves, los rendimientos de referencia de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos subieron ligeramente, situándose cerca de máximos de varios años, mientras que los de la deuda a dos años, que suelen reflejar las expectativas sobre las tasas de la Fed, tuvieron un alza más marcada. El Promedio Industrial Dow Jones (.DJI) cayó 34,69 puntos, o un 0,07%, a 51.145,18 unidades, mientras que el S&P 500 (.SPX) perdió 47,95 puntos, o un 0,61%, a 7.753,82. El Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) retrocedió 378,50 puntos, o un 1,37%, a 27.160,19. Entre los 11 sectores principales del S&P 500, los valores energéticos (.SPNY) lideraron las subidas porcentuales, mientras que el sector tecnológico (.SPLRCT) , lastrado por los chips, sufrió la mayor caída.

item.title: Trump administration freezes green cards for Microsoft, IT firms, probes universities
item.description: The US suspended Microsoft , major IT outsourcers and software maker Adobe from a key green-card program on Thursday while opening probes into nine top universities, widening a crackdown it says targets fraud and protects American jobs.
item.dc:creator: Akash Sriram, Steve Holland
item.content:encoded: The US suspended Microsoft (MSFT.O) , major IT outsourcers and software maker Adobe (ADBE.O) from a key green-card program on Thursday while opening probes into nine top universities, widening a crackdown it says targets fraud and protects American jobs. Since taking office, US President Donald Trump has pursued a broad effort to reduce the number of foreign-born people in the US and curtail their pathway to residence and citizenship. Thursday's twin actions mark the broadest strike yet against skilled-worker immigration programs — potentially cutting off a common path to permanent residency for foreign tech workers — while putting some of the country's top research universities on notice. "There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused the system more than Microsoft," Vice President JD Vance said. He said the company laid off 6,000 American workers last year while benefiting from 6,300 H-1B temporary worker visas and nearly 3,000 green cards. His comments came hours before Trump honored tech billionaires for their contributions to America, including Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. Nadella once held an H-1B visa, as did Elon Musk, who was also honored, while three of the other CEOs honored are immigrants. Nadella thanked Trump for the medal, saying in a post on X he would continue to advance technology and drive American prosperity. Microsoft is the largest filer of PERM applications, or the [USN:L4N45U1DA TEXT:"permanent labor certification"] process, according to data from the US labor department. Under PERM, which most employment-based green cards require, employers must show a foreign hire will not hurt US workers' wages or jobs. The company said in a statement that about 80% of the H-1B applications it filed in the last fiscal year were to extend or change the status of current employees, not to hire new workers. In July, the company said it would [USN:L4N4380XC TEXT:"cut 4,800 jobs"], or about 2.1% of its global workforce. CRACKDOWN WIDENS Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling said the suspension would also cover Cognizant (CTSH.O) , Infosys (INFY.NS) , Tata Consultancy Services (TCS.NS) , Wipro (WIPR.NS) , HCL Technologies (HCLT.NS) and Capgemini (CAPP.PA) . "We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent labor certification applications involving these companies," Sonderling said. He said these companies had since 2009 sought almost three million foreign workers, and had received over 230,000 H-1B visa approvals and over 100,000 permanent labor certifications. Amazon.com was the largest employer of approved H-1B beneficiaries in fiscal 2026, followed by Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys, Apple and Microsoft, according to US immigration data. Vance said the suspensions would last "as long as it needs to," and that the administration wanted the companies to change how they hire. He said some companies post ineffective job ads, then point to the lack of applicants to justify hiring lower-paid foreign workers. Microsoft said in its statement that it pays its H-1B employees the same as any other employees doing comparable work. Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, HCL Technologies, Wipro and Capgemini did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Tata Consultancy Services declined to comment. Nasscom, India's IT industry body, said Indian tech companies in the US had significantly reduced their reliance on H-1B visas, and relatively few of their workers sought green cards through the PERM process. In September last year, the Labor Department launched an enforcement drive called "Project Firewall" as a White House proclamation imposed a one-time $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions for workers hired from abroad. UNIVERSITIES UNDER SCRUTINY Vance also said nine universities, including Harvard, Yale and Stanford, would be investigated for what the administration called the misuse of exchange-visitor visas to undercut American wages. The nine schools also include Brown and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Labor Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito said subpoenas had already been served. D'Esposito said investigators would examine whether foreign influence, improper financial relationships or visa abuse were compromising federally funded research. “It could have an enormous economic impact on the whole US economy,” said Sarah Spreitzer, a vice president at the American Council on Education, which represents college and university presidents. International students historically spent $40 billion a year while in the US, she said. The probe deepens the administration's [USN:L1N45M14M TEXT:"long-running fight"] with Harvard over foreign students. Last year, the Department of Homeland Security subpoenaed the university over alleged misconduct by international students and its compliance with immigration law. Harvard called that subpoena "unfounded retribution" but said it would comply as far as the law requires. Rapidly changing visa policies caused a sharp drop in international applications to Columbia University and contributed to the university pausing admissions to one of its journalism programs, Reuters reported last week.

item.title: Starbucks declines comment on Chipotle takeover report, says laser focused on turnaround
item.description: Starbucks on Thursday declined to comment on a report that it had explored a takeover of Chipotle Mexican Grill , saying it was "laser focused" on its turnaround under CEO Brian Niccol.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Starbucks (SBUX.O) on Thursday declined to comment on a report that it had explored a takeover of Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG.N) , saying it was "laser focused" on its turnaround under CEO Brian Niccol. The Financial Times reported earlier that Starbucks had worked with advisers in recent months on a potential takeover of Chipotle, citing people familiar with the matter. Niccol ran Chipotle for about six years before taking the top job at Starbucks in 2024. Responding to the report, a Starbucks spokesperson said the company does not comment on rumors and speculation, adding that Starbucks remained focused on its two-year turnaround under Niccol and had strong momentum and confidence in its long-term growth potential. Chipotle did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. Starbucks, valued at about $107 billion, pared losses to close nearly flat on Thursday, while Chipotle shares jumped 6%, giving the burrito chain a market value of about $41 billion. At Chipotle, Niccol was credited with steering the company through the aftermath of its food-safety crises and expanding its digital business, helping drive years of strong sales growth. "For Chipotle, we think this would be viewed positively, primarily driven by Brian Niccol returning to the brand," RBC Capital Markets analyst Logan Reich said. Still, Reich said investors have been sceptical of restaurant companies buying additional brands to drive growth, adding that the strategic rationale for Starbucks acquiring Chipotle was unclear. POTENTIAL TAKEOVER COULD PROVE COSTLY A takeover could also prove costly for Starbucks as it invests heavily in its turnaround, analysts said. "A deal could require heavy borrowing or issuing shares," said Lale Akoner, global market strategist at eToro. "Without a compelling financial case, investors may view the deal as an expensive distraction." Over the past two years, Niccol has prioritized customer satisfaction through investments in staffing and store improvements aimed at reducing wait times and restoring the coffeehouse atmosphere that helped make the chain a global brand. The company has committed at least $500 million to labor investments as part of its overhaul, putting pressure on profitability. Starbucks has posted four consecutive quarters of comparable sales growth under Niccol, though he said [USN:L6N43V1FM TEXT:"in July"] that "we have more work to do." "The timing of this would be a little weird, given that Starbucks is in the middle of its transformation and hasn't yet shown the margin improvement investors are probably hoping for," said Brian Jacobsen, chief economic strategist at Annex Wealth Management. Starbucks' adjusted operating margin was 14.4% in the fiscal third quarter, down from 16.7% two years earlier, according to LSEG data. The company also said on Thursday that it looked forward to reporting fourth-quarter results and providing its outlook for the next fiscal year later this month. DEAL COULD BOOST CHIPOTLE'S INTERNATIONAL EXPANSION A deal could, however, help accelerate Chipotle's international expansion, analysts said. "What I like about this potential is the opportunity CEO Brian Niccol would have to leverage Starbucks' licensed partnerships in Europe to expand Chipotle more aggressively," Northcoast Research analyst Jim Sanderson said. International expansion has been a focus for Chipotle CEO Scott Boatwright, who succeeded Niccol. The company opened its first restaurants in Mexico and Saudi Arabia this year, adding to roughly 100 locations outside the United States. Chipotle also announced a joint venture last year with South Korean food company SPC Group to expand in Asia. Starbucks has roughly 40,000 stores worldwide. In the United States, Chipotle had 3,938 restaurants as of last year, while Starbucks has about 18,000 stores in North America, according to the companies' annual reports.

item.title: Maduro y Cilia Flores son acusados en EEUU por presuntos actos de tortura en Venezuela
item.description: El expresidente venezolano Nicolás Maduro y su esposa, Cilia Flores, fueron acusados el jueves de un nuevo delito en Estados Unidos, derivado de los cargos de que torturaron a opositores y ciudadanos estadounidense para mantener al país bajo su control.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El expresidente venezolano Nicolás Maduro y su esposa, Cilia Flores, fueron acusados el jueves de un nuevo delito en Estados Unidos, derivado de los cargos de que torturaron a opositores y ciudadanos estadounidense para mantener al país bajo su control. Maduro y Flores fueron acusados de conspiración para cometer tortura, lo que se suma a los cargos de tráfico de drogas a los que ya se enfrentaban, según una querella sustitutiva presentada ante el tribunal federal de Manhattan. De ser declarados culpables, Maduro y Flores se enfrentarían a una pena mínima obligatoria de 50 años de prisión. Flores, de 69 años, y Maduro, de 63, fueron detenidos por el ejército estadounidense el 3 de enero en Caracas y trasladados a Nueva York para responder a los cargos de narcotráfico. La redada sorpresa puso fin a los 13 años de mandato de Maduro en Venezuela, que desde entonces ha intensificado la cooperación con Estados Unidos bajo el liderazgo de la exvicepresidenta de Maduro, Delcy Rodríguez. Maduro y Flores se declararon inocentes de los cargos de tráfico de drogas y permanecen recluidos en el Centro de Detención Metropolitano de Brooklyn desde su captura. Su juicio está previsto para el 1 de junio de 2027. Los fiscales afirmaron que Maduro ordenó en 2013 el arresto de un oficial militar venezolano al que sospechaba de planear un golpe de Estado. Según los fiscales, miembros de la dirección de contrainteligencia militar de Venezuela interrogaron al oficial mientras le aplicaban descargas eléctricas con un cable con corriente unas 20 veces y lo colgaban de las manos y los pies durante varios minutos seguidos. En 2022, un ciudadano estadounidense detenido al entrar en Venezuela fue acusado de conspirar para asesinar a Maduro y fue torturado por oficiales de contrainteligencia militar mediante palizas y descargas eléctricas en los brazos, las piernas y los genitales, según la acusación. Desde su captura y arresto, el Departamento de Justicia de Estados Unidos "ha estado trabajando para descubrir el alcance de sus presuntos crímenes contra el pueblo de Venezuela y de Estados Unidos", dijo el fiscal general Todd Blanche en una publicación en redes sociales. Los abogados de Maduro no respondieron de inmediato a la solicitud de comentarios. Durante la audiencia judicial del jueves sobre la solicitud de Flores para ser puesta en libertad, su abogado, Mark Donnelly, dijo que no había tenido tiempo de repasar los nuevos cargos con su clienta. No se le pidió a Flores que se declarara culpable o inocente. NIEGAN A FLORES LIBERTAD BAJO FIANZA Los abogados de Flores argumentaron que su clienta necesita un procedimiento cardíaco y desea recuperarse en un entorno más cómodo. Propusieron trasladarla a una residencia en el área de la ciudad de Nueva York con seguridad privada las 24 horas y afirmaron que no representa un peligro para la comunidad. Al denegar la solicitud de libertad bajo fianza, Hellerstein consideró que las pruebas contra Flores parecían contundentes. El juez también señaló que Flores, quien vestía una camiseta oscura de prisión y auriculares para escuchar la traducción simultánea al español del proceso, parecía gozar de buena salud. "Para lo que valga, su aspecto hoy no es peor, y quizás sea un poco mejor, que cuando me reuní con ella por primera vez en su comparecencia ante el juez", dijo Hellerstein, refiriéndose a su primera comparecencia ante el tribunal el 5 de enero. "Todavía tenía vendajes de la invasión militar", señaló por su parte Donnelly. Los fiscales de la Fiscalía Federal de Manhattan se opusieron a la liberación de Flores. Argumentaron que ha recibido atención médica adecuada en el centro de detención y que, de ser liberada, representa un riesgo "extremo" de fuga y un peligro para el público, incluyendo la posible intimidación de testigos. La negativa por parte de Hellerstein no afectará al juicio de Flores ni a su posible condena.

item.title: Five charts sounding the alarm for stretched US markets: McGeever
item.description: US stocks and bonds currently appear highly stretched on several key measures, suggesting investors should tread with extreme caution. The big question is whether we may be at, or near, an inflection point.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded: US stocks and bonds currently appear highly stretched on several key measures, suggesting investors should tread with extreme caution. The big question is whether we may be at, or near, an inflection point. Wall Street's record-breaking highs mask historic levels of concentration and narrow breadth. Treasury yields are now so high that, depending on your perspective, they either represent a generational buying opportunity or are about to send the equity rally screeching into reverse. Meanwhile, the spiking “term premium” could slam both stocks and bonds. But does that indicate mean reversion is just around the corner? It’s tough to say. Historically high AI-related profits and healthy economic growth could maintain Wall Street's bull run for months if not years, and there's no shortage of reasons why yields cannot rise further, and not all of them are negative. Below are five charts that bring this debate into focus: Stock market concentration Tech and AI stocks now comprise over 40% of the S&P 500's (.SPX) market cap. That's higher than the peak of the dotcom bubble in early 2000. Add in AI-related companies, and tech's footprint tops 50%, also a record. This level of concentration is fine when tech is surging, but concerns are mounting about the AI revolution, including safety issues and doubts over the technology's long-term economic viability. A turn in AI sentiment could spark a serious correction. On the other hand, if the hundreds of billions of dollars in AI investment start to pay off, the rally could get supercharged. Equal weight under-performance The current ratio of the equal-weighted S&P 500 index to the market cap-weighted index is collapsing, based on Invesco's RSP EW exchange-traded fund and the SPY ETF. In plain English, the main US index in which stocks have equal weighting is under-performing the more widely followed index by the widest margin in 24 years. That’s almost entirely due to the strong performance of tech and AI names, suggesting corporate America overall is not quite as strong as the record-breaking S&P 500 headlines suggest. Equity risk premium Investors usually demand a higher rate of return when buying “riskier” stocks versus traditionally “safe” bonds. This difference between the earnings yield on stocks and the 10-year Treasury yield is referred to as the “equity risk premium”. It is currently the lowest in 24 years and is actually negative – a very rare occurrence this century. This should be a signal for investors to start rethinking the size of their equity allocation, though, as of now, we certainly aren’t seeing many signs of that. Real yields The yield on 30-year Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) is nearing 3.40%, the highest since 2002. That represents the near-guaranteed inflation-adjusted – or “real” – annual rate of return investors can now lock in for the next 30 years. Again, one might expect that to pull capital away from equities and help prop up the ailing bond market, especially as rising real yields are usually indicative of stronger economic growth. Spiking yields should also negatively impact corporate borrowers at some point – the question is when that might be. Term premium Last but not least, the “term premium” – the market’s wild card. This is the estimated level of extra compensation investors demand in return for buying long-dated Treasuries over short-term debt. What’s pushing up the term premium remains an open question – it could be growing doubts around Fed credibility, US debt debasement fears, or something else entirely. But no matter the cause, the main concern with the term premium is always whether it’s rising or not. If it is, it's potentially a signal of more fundamental problems that could have serious economic and market consequences. And right now it's rising sharply.
